title: Fed’s Logan favours at least two hikes, says pace could quicken
article:
(Nov 11): Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas president Lorie Logan said she still sees the need for at least two quarter-point rate increases, but that the pace of those hikes may need to be quicker than the Fed is moving this fall.

“It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases,” Logan said on Tuesday in prepared remarks for a conference in Houston, referring to the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on which she votes this year.

While the pace of hikes will depend on economic data and financial conditions, “It may be possible to move more rapidly this winter than the FOMC has moved so far this fall,” Logan added.

Fed officials left interest rates unchanged at their Oct 27-28 meeting after raising them by a quarter percentage point in September. That was the first rate hike since 2023 as policymakers seek to cool inflation that has been above their 2% target for more than five years.

A majority of officials in September signalled at least one more rate increase would be necessary this year, according to their median projection. While several Fed officials have reinforced this view in recent remarks and said hikes can come at a gradual pace, governor Christopher Waller earlier on Tuesday said the Fed should consider raising rates by a larger, half percentage point at its next meeting in December.

A report released on Tuesday morning showed the consumer price index rose by more than expected in October, with core inflation accelerating at a 0.3% pace from a month earlier. Logan said she’s concerned the Fed’s preferred gauge for inflation, due later this month, could show a similar pickup for October.

title: IBM to end immigration sponsorship for roles in biggest unit
article:
(Nov 11): International Business Machines Corp (IBM) is ending immigration sponsorship for some roles in its largest division following a crackdown by the Trump administration on a visa programme that’s been a talent pipeline for the tech industry.

“We have opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles in IBM Consulting,” an IBM spokesperson said.

Impacted workers can continue working with IBM outside the US, or leave the company at the end of the year, according to a document shared with managers this week in that division seen by Bloomberg. Consulting is by far IBM’s largest division, with over 150,000 workers, according to its website.

The technology industry’s reliance on foreign workers has long been a flashpoint in the debate over immigration. Since President Donald Trump’s return to office last year, the administration has seized on those concerns and pressed tech giants to do more to train and hire US workers.

As part of that effort, Trump has moved to make it harder for companies to use H-1B visas to attract foreign talent. The changes have included proposals for US$100,000 filing fees for most candidates and tightening the rules of how the H-1B visas are awarded in an annual lottery, giving priority to companies offering the highest salaries.

See also: US stocks slide after hot inflation boosts December rate hike bets

Last month the administration accused Microsoft Corp, Adobe Inc and a half-dozen other companies of abusing a US worker visa programme and suspended them indefinitely from using it.

The affected IBM division participated “US high-skilled visa programmes” to address skill shortages, the spokesperson said. But participation has been declining for a number of years and skill availability and client need have evolved, the spokesperson said.

Big Blue has refashioned itself as a high-growth software company through major acquisitions of Red Hat, HashiCorp and Confluent. At the same time, its consulting business has lagged — the division’s growth has been largely flat since 2024.

Hilton to make Canberra debut with 184-room hotel in Manuka
article:
Hilton has signed Hilton Canberra Manuka, a 184-room hotel that will mark the group’s entry into Australia’s capital. It is expected to open in early 2027.

The hotel will be at 15–17 Franklin Street in the established Manuka precinct, about a 10-minute drive from Canberra’s city centre. It is directly opposite Manuka Oval, the city’s main cricket and Australian rules football grounds.

The hotel will carry Hilton’s flagship Hilton Hotels & Resorts brand and operate under a franchise agreement with ICC Development Group, an Australian developer focused on hotel and mixed-use projects.

The group is handling the hotel development on behalf of the Liangis family, a prominent Canberra family known for commercial property development and other business ventures.

The 184-room property offers eight suites. Standard rooms range from 344 to 484 sq ft.

Facilities include an executive lounge, an all-day dining restaurant and bar, fitness and wellness facilities, sauna and pool. A ballroom and a multifunction space, that can be divided into four rooms, will cater to events.

The hotel is part of a broader development that will also include ground-level retail, additional dining venues and a cinema.

Situated in a key location, the hotel will target government, corporate, diplomatic, sporting and leisure travellers. The property is close to Parliament House, the Parliamentary Triangle, Canberra’s embassy district, the Barton business precinct, and attractions such as the National Gallery of Australia, the National Museum of Australia and Questacon, Australia’s national science centre.

The city’s railway station is about 1.5km away, and its airport some 7km away.

“The signing of Hilton Canberra Manuka represents an important milestone in Hilton’s growth across Australasia and brings our flagship brand to Australia’s national capital,” said Tushar Raniga, director of development at Hilton Australasia.

Harrold Dakin, CEO of ICC Development Group, said the project represents a significant private investment by the Liangis family in Canberra’s tourism and hospitality sector.

The hotel is expected to support about 100 to 120 full-time, part-time and casual positions, as well as demand for the precinct’s restaurants, cafés and retailers.

The hotel will be part of Hilton Honors, the group’s loyalty programme.

Members who book directly through preferred Hilton channels get perks such as member discounts and complimentary standard WiFi. They can also use the Hilton Honors app for check-in, room selection and Digital Key, where available.

Hilton has more than 9,600 properties across 28 brands in 144 countries and territories.

title: Flight to quality to support demand for high-spec industrial spaces; rents to stay stable in 2027: Realion
article:
The Singapore industrial real estate market may see rents stabilise in 2027, as rising supply coincides with sustained demand for high-specification industrial spaces, according to research by Realion (OrangeTee and ETC) Group.

In a research report on its outlook for 2027, the firm notes that the industrial property market has stayed resilient this year, despite geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and increased tariffs.

In 3Q2026, the JTC all-industrial rental index rose 0.5% q-o-q, marking a 24th consecutive quarter of increase. On a y-o-y basis, the index grew 2.1%. Industrial property prices also increased, rising 1% q-o-q and 4.2% y-o-y.

Given the resilient performance, Realion is projecting rents to grow between 1.8% and 3% for the whole of 2026, with the higher end of the range marginally exceeding the 2.4% growth recorded in 2025.

Industrial property prices are expected to grow between 3% and 4% this year, slightly lower than the 5% increase logged in 2025.

Going into 2027, Realion believes high-spec industrial spaces will see sustained demand as occupiers become more selective.

“As flight to quality takes precedence, some industrialists will continue to prioritise quality facilities, driven by technological advancements, sustainability, ESG compliance and supply-chain shifts,” the report states.

The demand for high-spec buildings is also being supported by the ongoing AI boom. Singapore’s established semiconductor and advanced manufacturing ecosystem, coupled with its skilled talent pool, is expected to continue creating opportunities for specialised industrial properties that support high-tech manufacturing, semiconductor production and other AI-related supply chains.

At the same time, the market is seeing rising supply. Based on planning approvals as of September this year, around 2.7 million sq ft of  industrial gross floor area is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter, while another 12.3 million sq ft is slated to come online in 2027.

The higher supply will place pressure on the overall market, though Realion expects prices and rents for high-spec spaces to remain bolstered by flight-to-quality-driven demand.

Non-high spec and older industrial properties, however, are likely to face rental and price pressure amid the increased supply. In addition, some low-margin production may continue to be shifted to lower-cost neighbouring countries, creating further headwinds for certain industrial properties such as landed factories, Realion adds.

Given the countervailing factors, Realion estimates industrial property rental growth could stabilise at a range of 1% to 3% in 2027, on a par with its projection for 2026. Industrial leasing volume is predicted at around 12,500 to 15,500 for next year, similar to the 13,000 to 15,000 range forecast for 2026.

Realion is also forecasting industrial property prices to grow by 2% to 4% for 2027, on the back of a resale volume of 1,500 to 2,300 units. This is roughly on a par with the 3% to 4% growth and 1,800 to 2,000 resale volume it projects for 2026.

title: Two freehold Camden Park bungalow plots for sale at $26 mil and $27 mil
article:
Two adjacent freehold sites in the Camden Park Good Class Bungalow (GCB) area are being offered for sale through an expression of interest (EOI) exercise. The residential sites, which each house a single-storey detached bungalow, are located at 15 and 15A Camden Park.

The sites are held under separate titles by the same owner, and are being offered for sale individually, marketing agent CBRE said in a Nov 10 release. Offers may be submitted for either property or for both.

The site at 15 Camden Park spans a land area of 13,116 sq ft and has a guide price of $26 million, or $1,982 psf. The site at 15A Camden Park measures 14,060 sq ft and is priced at $27 million, or $1,920 psf.

Each plot could potentially be redeveloped into “a substantial family residence”, said Rowena Chan, senior vice president of residential capital markets, Singapore at CBRE.

“Their adjoining location also provides an additional option for buyers seeking a larger landholding or wishing to establish neighbouring family homes,” she added.

Subject to prevailing planning requirements, site conditions and relevant approvals, the adjoining titles may be acquired together as a combined 27,176 sq ft holding.

According to CBRE, the properties were formerly the residence of the late Earnest Lau and Kwa Geok Lian.

Located in the Camden Park landed residential enclave in Bukit Timah, the sites are less than 1km from the Singapore Botanic Gardens, while the Botanic Gardens MRT Interchange (serving the Circle and Downtown lines) is also within walking distance.

The Camden Park area has 26 homes, with landholdings in the enclave averaging at approximately 22,605 sq ft, said CBRE.

As such, the properties at 15 and 15A Camden Park each offer “the prestige and privacy of a GCB area address at a more manageable overall investment quantum”, the firm added.

Caveats lodged show that the most recent transaction in Camden Park was for a detached house on a 29,922 sq ft freehold plot that fetched $48 million ($1,604 psf) in November 2025.

Before that, the last transaction occurred in September 2021, when a freehold detached home occupying a 16,607 sq ft site changed hands for $32.5 million ($1,957 psf).

The EOI will close at 5pm on Jan 20, 2027.

title: Tampines Mall completes $24 mil asset enhancement initiative
article:
Tampines Mall is completing its $24 million asset enhancement initiative (AEI) in December, marking a new chapter for the eight-storey shopping centre in the Tampines Regional Centre.

The mall, owned by CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (CICT), began the AEI in September 2025 to improve about 50,000 sq ft of net lettable area.

In its 3Q2026 financial update, published on Oct 29, CICT said around 97% of the AEI space is committed or in advanced negotiation as of Sept 30.

In a separate Nov 10 release, Tampines Mall said the transformation introduces 21 new brands, including 15 making their debut in the East. The mall now houses over 160 stores, with a net lettable area exceeding 356,000 sq ft.

“The refreshed Tampines Mall brings together a broad mix of premium, accessible-luxury and everyday brands, alongside dining, sports and lifestyle offerings and well-loved favourites,” added Adrian Lai, general manager of Tampines Mall.

A highlight of the revamped mall is a beauty cluster with 14 brands, including Sephora.

The beauty retailer, which previously operated at neighbouring shopping centre Tampines 1 now occupies ground-floor space that was formerly part of Isetan. The Japanese department store closed its Tampines Mall outlet in November 2025 after 30 years.

Other brands in the beauty cluster include new-to-Tampines Mall names such as British skincare brand Elemis, Chinese makeup retailer Judydoll, Dutch home and body cosmetics brand Rituals, as well as luxury brand YSL Beauty.

In addition, beauty brands such as Shiseido and Chanel, which previously operated through store concessions within Isetan, have opened standalone boutiques in the mall.

Another highlight of the AEI is a refresh of the dining line-up at Tampinese Mall. New additions include Italian dining concept Casa Vostra, Chinese milk tea brand Charlie’s Tea, Hong Kong-founded Ging Sun Ho King of Bun and specialty coffee shop Alchemist.

The mall has also expanded its jewellery and fashion offerings. Key changes include Decathlon, which closed their click-and-collect store at Tampines Mall at the start of the year. The French sports retailer is moving into a more spacious 18,000 sq ft store on Level 2 that will open in December.

Other new names include German leather goods store Braun Büffel, international fashion brand Meilleur Moment, watch dealer Vincent Watch and travel accessories store Boarding Gate.

Tampines Mall first opened in 1995. It is adjacent to the Tampines MRT interchange (serving the East-West and Downtown lines) and the Tampines Bus Interchange. It also neighbours two other malls, Century Square and Tampines 1, which are both owned by Frasers Centrepoint Trust.

title: Could mortgage rates rise further? What bank packages in Singapore are signalling after Fed hike
article:
On Sept 16, the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023. Within days, Singapore banks pulled their fixed-rate packages, repriced them outside their usual schedule, and brought them back at higher rates.

So, will rates keep rising? No one can say for sure, but today’s bank packages offer a useful clue.

What bank packages are telling us

When a bank fixes your rate, it locks in its own funding cost for the same period.

What that costs depends on where the market expects Sora — the key interest rate benchmark for floating-rate home loans in Singapore — to go.

That’s why the difference between a bank’s three-year and two-year fixed rates, known as the spread, is worth watching.

If banks expect rates to rise, fixing for three years costs them more, so the three-year rate is priced higher and the spread widens. If they expect rates to stay stable, the spread stays narrow. And if they expect rates to fall, the three-year rate can even come in cheaper than the two-year rate.

Fixed rates have risen by 0.30–0.77 percentage points (refer to Table 1). For most home loans, the three-year rate is now slightly above the two-year rate. The exception is the $300,000 HDB loan, where the three-year rate is cheaper.

Things get more interesting, however, when we look at how the spreads have changed.

As Table 2 shows, the gap between three-year and two-year rates has narrowed for half of the packages. Where the spread has widened, the increase is small, at 0.12 percentage point or less.

This may indicate that rates could stay at this level for now or mildly rise, rather than climb sharply.

What the Fed is signalling

After raising rates in September, the Fed held them steady at its October meeting, but its latest statement leaves the door open to another rise.

About 76% of experts expect one more hike before the end of the year, according to CNBC's latest Fed Survey of fund managers, strategists and economists.

If that happens, expect the same pattern in Singapore as the previous time: Sora will likely move first. Whether fixed rates follow depends on how much of a higher Sora banks have already priced in.

Fixed rates are up 0.30 to 0.77 percentage points, and with the spread narrowing for half of the packages. This could indicate that banks expect rates to stay stable or rise only modestly from here.

These are indicators, not predictions. Fed projections can shift quickly, and banks can reprice their packages at any time. Treat this as context for your own decision rather than financial advice.

What has happened since the Fed hike

1. Sora moved before the Fed did.

Sora is the average rate banks charge each other to borrow Singapore dollars overnight, and most floating home loans are pegged to it.

Singapore rates tend to follow US rates because money moves freely in and out of the country, though the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s management of the Singapore dollar, and factors like large capital inflows, soften the link.

Banks also price in what they expect, so Sora started drifting up months before the Fed moved.

The monthly average Sora went from about 1.00% in April to 1.27% in August, and averaged about 1.34% in October. On a $500,000 floating loan, a 0.27 percentage point rise works out to roughly $110 a month more in interest in the early years.

2. Floating loans are still catching up.

Most floating loans use the three-month Sora — an average of daily Sora over the past three months — so it catches up with the daily rate slowly.

The three-month Sora hit a low of 1.02% on 29 April, was 1.20% the day before the Fed's announcement, and has reached 1.32% as at the time of writing (based on data as at Nov 9), 55 days later. If your loan is pegged to it, you're likely paying for the summer rise with a delay.

Singapore benchmark rates: Daily Sora and three-month compounded Sora:

3. Fixed packages were pulled, then repriced.

A fixed rate is a commitment: once it is agreed, the bank is stuck with it, even if its own costs rise.

So, after the Fed's move on Sept 16, banks withdrew packages first and repriced them after (see Table 3), according to Cashew’s internal bank package data.

What this could mean for you

• If you're on a three-month Sora floating loan, expect the lag. The rise in the daily Sora is still feeding through the three-month average. Your rate won't jump sharply, but it may keep inching up for a few months, even if the headlines go quiet.

• If you're shopping for a fixed rate, treat pre-September rates as out of date. Packages have already been repriced higher, and many ads are still showing old rates.

• A rate isn't yours until it's approved. Packages are first come, first served, and they can change while your application waits in the queue.

• Don't panic. Over the life of your loan, rates will go up and down many times. If you switch to the lowest rate whenever your lock-in ends, you shouldn't overpay in the long run. You can do that by repricing (moving to a new package with your current bank) or refinancing (moving your loan to another bank)

The Fed’s September hike has already reshaped the market. Banks have repriced already, and Sora is still catching up.

But today's bank packages suggest rates may hold steady or rise only mildly from here, rather than climb sharply.

Whether you’re on a floating rate, coming to the end of a lock-in period, or buying your first home, what matters most is acting on current rates, not old ones. Compare your options early and make sure you’re on the lowest package available to you.

title: High Payouts vs. Value Traps: How to Screen the Top 5 SGX Yielders
article:
A quick scan of the SGX turns up yields that appear far more attractive than Central Provident Fund (CPF) savings or Treasury bills (T-bills).
But a
high yield
can mean two things.
With strong fundamentals, it can be an income opportunity backed by sustainable cash generation and room for dividend growth.
With weakening fundamentals, it can be a value trap, with dividend cut risk and further share-price downside.
A falling share price can inflate yields even as earnings and cash flow deteriorate.
For income investors, the task is separating genuine opportunities from
dividend traps
.
We screen five high-yielding stocks to see what supports their payouts and what puts them at risk.

*Note: Share prices as at 6 Nov 2026.
Keppel Infrastructure Trust (SGX: A7RU), or KIT
KIT owns essential infrastructure, from wind farms to gas pipelines, and its payouts are supported by long-term contracts with cost pass-through.
Its trailing 12-month distribution per unit (DPU) is S$0.0396, which has grown about 1% a year, giving a yield of 8.1% at a unit price of S$0.49 as at 6 November 2026.
Interest cover is 8.3 times, about 79% of debt is fixed and FY2026 refinancing is secured.
Future growth is expected from a subsea cable vessel due to enter service around end-2026, bolt-on acquisitions at Ixom and Ventura, and about S$700 million of debt capacity for acquisitions.
KIT’s distributions are backed by recurring cash flows, but net gearing rose to 44.2% from 38.7% at the end of 2025, so further debt-funded deals need watching.
Genting Singapore Limited (SGX: G13)
Genting Singapore operates Resorts World Sentosa (RWS), an integrated resort with casino gaming.
Its annual dividend of S$0.04 gives a yield of about 6.6% at a share price of S$0.61 as at 6 November 2026.
The balance sheet is strong, with S$2.9 billion in cash and no bank borrowings.
However, 1H2026 free cash flow was only S$21.1 million against the S$241.8 million FY2025 final dividend paid in the same half.
Capex is high because of RWS 2.0, which is scheduled for completion in 2030.
Moderating tourism arrivals, measured consumer spending and RWS 2.0 redevelopment weigh on profit and cash flow now, with longer stays and more non-gaming spending as the intended payoff.
While the dividend yield looks attractive and the cash pile is solid, the business environment and RWS 2.0 are worth watching.
Asian Pay Television Trust (SGX: S7OU), or APTT
APTT owns Taiwan Broadband Communications, a cable operator across five Taiwan franchise areas where about 90% of its revenue is subscription-based.
Its FY2026 distribution guidance of S$0.0080 per unit is 24% below FY2025’s S$0.0105.
At a unit price of S$0.07 as at 6 November 2026, that is a forward yield of 11.4%.
Both revenue and EBITDA have been falling as cheaper IPTV and streaming pull subscribers from basic cable TV faster than the broadband income can grow.
Net debt was 7.6 times EBITDA as at 31 March 2026, and about 25% of debt is unhedged.
As at 30 June 2026, cash was S$48.7 million against S$1.07 billion of gross debt.
Operating cash flow of S$63.4 million covers the S$9.5 million paid to unitholders more than six times.
If EBITDA keeps falling, debt repayment competes with the distribution, and the high yield suggests the market expects DPU to fall.
Sasseur Real Estate Investment Trust (SGX: CRPU)
Sasseur REIT owns four outlet malls in Chongqing, Hefei and Kunming.
At a unit price of S$0.63 as at 6 November 2026, it trades at 0.77 times its net asset value of S$0.82, for a trailing distribution yield of 10.2%.
DPU rose 10.2% to S$0.03366 in 1H2026.
Rent has a fixed component that rises 3% a year and a variable part tied to outlet sales, which grew 7.4% in 1H2026 but only 2.1% in the second quarter.
Occupancy slipped to 97.2% in 2Q2026 from 98.5% in 1Q2026 as the Hefei outlet reconfigured its tenants.
No tenant is above 5% of gross revenue, but leases are short, with 56.7% of gross revenue expiring in 2026.
Gearing is 25.6%, interest cover is 5.6 times and all loans are in renminbi, matching its renminbi income.
The yield is largely protected by low debt, and the risks to watch are short leases and slowing sales.
Singapore Airlines Limited (SGX: C6L), or SIA
SIA is Singapore’s flagship carrier, and FY2025/2026 was a strong year.
Operating profit rose 39% to S$2.4 billion on higher yields and lower fuel costs.
Its FY2025/2026 dividend was S$0.37, down from S$0.40, made up of S$0.27 in ordinary and S$0.10 in special dividends.
At S$6.95 as at 6 November 2026, the yield is 5.3%.
Excluding the special dividend, the yield is 3.9%, a better guide to what SIA can sustain.
Free cash flow of about S$2.5 billion covered the roughly S$1.2 billion payout twice over.
Jet fuel prices then surged on the Middle East conflict.
In 1QFY2026/2027, net fuel cost rose 78.5%, leading to a S$76 million net loss.
Cash of S$9.1 billion covers the gap for now, though debt edged up to S$10.7 billion.
In this case, a dividend funded by peak-cycle profits can look safer than it really is.
Get Smart: Don’t Let the Yield Fool You
High yields can be attractive, but an investor needs to judge each payout by the quality of its earnings,
cash flows
, balance sheet and future prospects.
KIT and Sasseur REIT have contracted or growing income supporting their payouts, though gearing and short leases need watching.
Genting Singapore paid out far more than its free cash flow, while APTT has already cut its distribution, and SIA’s payout depends on fuel prices.
Some yields are high because the market expects a cut, as APTT’s guidance shows.
Hence, a yield only matters if the company can continue to sustain or grow its dividends.

title: 3 US Stocks Down 30% – Are They Worth a Look?
article:
As tech leaders fall sharply from their peaks, investors are split on what to do next.
Some see it as a long-awaited Wall Street sale to grab a piece of these
tech titans
on the cheap.
Others contemplate a possible value trap.
Three technology leaders –
Alphabet Inc.
(NASDAQ: GOOGL),
Fortinet Inc.
(NASDAQ: FTNT), and
Broadcom Inc.
(NASDAQ: AVGO) – have seen roughly 30% of their equity values wiped out from the recent pullbacks.
Let’s unpack the insights behind their massive stock rout.
Alphabet: Capex Anxiety Meets Cloud Growth
Alphabet’s share price pulled back sharply from its peak of more than US$400 in May 2026 to around US$280, wiping out close to one-third of its market capitalisation.
The catalyst?
Earnings per share (EPS) missed in the third quarter of 2026 (3Q2026), coming in at US$2.12 against consensus analyst estimates of US$3.02.
As Alphabet owns a stake in the publicly listed SpaceX, a fall in the share price of the latter caused a non-operating accounting loss of US$8.7 billion for the quarter, which weighed on the bottom line.
Furthermore, Alphabet’s heavy capital outlays spooked investors, as it announced 3Q2026 quarterly capex of US$51.4 billion, pushing its free cash flow (FCF) to negative US$9.1 billion.
Although Alphabet’s 2026 capex is expected to stay within the guided range of US$195 billion to US$205 billion, capex spending in 2027 is projected to increase significantly, fuelling investors’ concerns.
However, Alphabet’s operating engines remain strong.
Its 3Q2026 revenue surged 25% year on year (YoY) to US$127.6 billion, driven by Google Cloud, which climbed 103% to US$30.7 billion.
Meanwhile, operating income increased 30% YoY to US$40.58 billion, with the operating margin improving from 31% to 32%, demonstrating improving operating leverage.
Right now, the market is offering Alphabet’s shares at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 13x – a significant discount relative to its
Magnificent Seven
peers, which trade at a median P/E of 31.6x.
Fortinet: Bottom-line Momentum Persists Despite Rising Costs
Fortinet share price has fallen around 30% despite the global cybersecurity company’s 3Q2026 revenue expanding 20% YoY to US$2.08 billion.
The revenue growth was driven by a 37% surge in product revenue to US$765 million, anchored by the growth in secure networking hardware and term licences.
Meanwhile, service revenue grew 13% to US$1.31 billion as the revenue for FortiGuard and other security subscription services was recognised.
Crucially, total gross margin contracted 1.8 percentage points to 79% as Fortinet shifts towards lower-margin product revenue, with the margin compression worsened by rising costs of memory chips and inventory-related expenses.
Moreover, although Fortinet is winning massive enterprise clients, these clients typically activate their services in phases, meaning the revenue is realised more slowly, exerting top-line pressure on Fortinet.
Still, Fortinet’s bottom-line momentum remains strong.
Its 3Q2026 operating income surged 29% to US$704.3 million and it delivered US$864.8 million in FCF. Fortinet demonstrated strong operating leverage as its top-line growth outpaced expense growth.
The verdict?
The latest sell-off reflects short-term market anxieties, rather than a structural decline of Fortinet’s business.
Broadcom: Valuation Reset vs Custom AI Dominance
From a peak of around US$490, Broadcom’s share price has dropped more than 30% to about US$330 per share, resetting its trailing P/E from over 70 to a more palatable level of over 40.
Still, investors should not ignore the custom chip designer’s concentration risk, with direct sales to one distributor accounting for 50% of its 3Q2026 net revenue.
In addition, its top five end customers account for approximately 55% of 3QFY2026 net revenue.
Despite these concentration risks, Broadcom remains dominant in custom chip design.
Revenue for its AI-driven Semiconductor Solutions segment skyrocketed 127% YoY to US$20.8 billion, lifting consolidated 3Q2026 revenue 85.5% YoY to US$29.59 billion, with an operating margin of 53.9%.
Backed by long-term demand from Big Tech firms such as Alphabet, Broadcom’s AI-led growth is expected to continue to 2031.
Crucially, Broadcom’s business is cash generative.
In the nine months ended 2 August 2026 (9MFY2026), Broadcom’s FCF increased 64.2% YoY to $31.9 billion – a stark contrast to hyperscalers alarming negative FCF.
The current valuation reset of a
cash-rich business
like Broadcom may make it worth a closer look for long-term investors.
Get Smart: Navigating Market Declines with Discipline
A 30% contraction is an opportunity, not necessarily to buy, but to analyse the reason behind it with discipline rather than emotions.
It’s easy to succumb to myopic market noise and lose sight of durable businesses that compound in value over time.
Amid market overreactions, Alphabet, Fortinet, and Broadcom display unique strengths.
Has the market bottomed? No one knows.
Smart investors know better than to time the bottom.
Instead, they buy in stages and track the operating metrics that truly matter.

title: 3 SGX Hidden Gems That Grew Profits by 24% (or More!)
article:
If you follow earnings season, you’ll know
blue chips
tend to hog the spotlight.
This time, some of the biggest profit gains came from much smaller companies.
Three Singapore-listed
small caps
grew their profits by 24% or more, and one more than doubled its bottom line.
If you invest for dividends, profit growth is a good start.
The cash behind it matters more.
One thing to keep in mind as you read: the three report over different periods, so watch the labels.
Can Tiong Woon keep raising its dividend?
Tiong Woon Corporation Holding Ltd
(SGX: BQM) is a one-stop integrated heavy-lift specialist with a presence in 12 countries.
Crane and transport hire makes up 96% of revenue.
For the financial year ended 30 June 2026 (FY2026), revenue rose 15% year on year (YoY) to S$187.7 million.
Profit attributable to shareholders climbed 24% to S$23.9 million.
The crane business drove the gains. Heavy Lift and Haulage external revenue grew 12% YoY, helped by Singapore, India and Brunei.
Gross margin widened to 40.7% from 37.6% on higher margins in that segment.
Turn to the cash flow statement, and you’ll see why Tiong Woon stands out.
Operating cash flow rose 31%, while capital expenditure nearly halved.
Free cash flow rose to S$43.7 million from S$6.3 million a year ago.
The board shared some of that cash.
It proposed a final dividend of S$0.025 per share, up 43% from S$0.0175.
You’ll still want to keep an eye on the balance sheet.
Tiong Woon held S$86.6 million in cash and bank deposits against S$108.0 million in borrowings, excluding lease liabilities.
The low capex bill may not last either. Management plans to keep renewing and expanding its fleet.
Demand looks supportive.
Tiong Woon cites official forecasts of Singapore construction demand of S$47 billion to S$53 billion in 2026, with Changi Airport Terminal 5 among the big projects.
Can Micro-Mechanics turn record profits into bigger dividends?
Micro-Mechanics (Holdings) Ltd
(SGX: 5DD) makes precision tools and parts used in semiconductor manufacturing.
For the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (1QFY2027) ended 30 September 2026, revenue rose 45.0% YoY to S$24.2 million, an all-time quarterly high.
Net profit rose 102.8% to S$6.4 million, also a quarterly record.
Wondering why profit grew faster than sales?
Look at the margins.
Gross margin widened to a 20-quarter high of 55.0%, from 51.5% a year ago.
Overheads fell to 20.7% of revenue from 25.1%.
In other words, more of each extra dollar of sales now reaches the bottom line.
Free cash flow moved the other way.
It fell 10.6% YoY to S$3.7 million.
Trade receivables rose in line with higher revenue, and the company paid more tax.
Capital expenditure also rose to S$0.9 million from S$0.3 million.
Should that worry you? Not much.
Micro-Mechanics had S$33.3 million in cash and no bank borrowings as at 30 September 2026.
No dividend was declared for the quarter, and that is normal since the company typically declares dividends in the second and fourth quarters.
Spending is the bigger question.
Micro-Mechanics expects to invest S$12 million in FY2027, including expanding its manufacturing footprint.
Under a five-year strategy, it wants to double revenue to at least S$150 million. That investment will compete with dividends for cash.
What’s missing from Civmec’s record quarter?
Civmec Limited
(SGX: P9D) is an integrated construction and engineering services provider to the energy, resources, infrastructure, and marine and defence sectors.
It is headquartered in Henderson, Western Australia and reports in Australian dollars.
For the first quarter of the fiscal year ending 30 June 2027 (1QFY2027), revenue rose 70.2% YoY to a record A$324 million.
Net profit after tax climbed 75.2% to A$18.4 million.
A significant uplift in activity in Civmec’s construction division drove the growth.
Work ramped up on BHP’s Port Debottlenecking Project 2 and Iluka Resources’ Eneabba Rare Earths Refinery.
The order book stood at around A$1.4 billion, up from A$1.15 billion a year ago.
Here’s the thing: the quarterly update did not include a cash flow statement or balance sheet.
You can’t see free cash flow, cash or debt for the quarter.
For a contractor, profit and cash can drift apart as big projects ramp up, so this is a real gap.
You should also note how thin the margins are.
Civmec’s net profit margin was 5.7%, against 5.5% a year ago.
That leaves little room for error on large projects.
No dividend was declared for the quarter.
Civmec paid a final dividend of A$0.035 on 23 October 2026.
Together with the A$0.025 interim, that took FY2026 dividends to A$0.060.
Get Smart: Check whether the cash followed the profit
Free cash flow
is the lifeblood of dividends.
So when a company posts a big profit gain, ask one more question: did the cash show up too?
Tiong Woon passes that test.
Profit grew 24%, while free cash flow rose almost sevenfold.
Micro-Mechanics doubled its profit, but free cash flow dipped as it invested more and waited on customer payments.
Civmec hasn’t shown its cash yet.
So the next time a small cap reports a record, open the cash flow statement before you get excited.
Profit that never turns into cash shouldn’t count for much in your dividend plans.

title: 4 Singapore Stocks I Would Buy if I Had S$30,000 to Spare
article:
Every investor with cash sitting on the sidelines asks themselves the same question: If I had fresh capital in my account today, where would I deploy it?
With S$30,000 ready to work in the Singapore market, swinging for the fences on a single stock is a fast track to striking out.
The smarter move is building a resilient, cash-generating portfolio designed to
compound
over time.
From steady dividend powerhouses to defensive market anchors, here are four core Singapore stocks to turn S$30,000 into a balanced, wealth-building engine.
How I Would Think About Allocating S$30,000
Putting S$30,000 into a single stock is like putting all your eggs in one basket: exciting when it works, but painful when it cracks.
I’d start with a steady
dividend
giant and a defensive grocery stock.
Those two are like a safety net, generating cash and holding steady if things get rocky.
Then I’d pick a proven market leader and a company with potential for a strong comeback.
That way, I get the chance for real growth without taking a risk on my whole stack.
This approach transforms S$30,000 into a well-rounded, wealth-building portfolio that can keep growing year after year.
DBS Group Holdings Ltd (SGX: D05) — The Dividend Anchor
When building a cash-generating portfolio, every investor needs an undeniable core heavyweight.
DBS Group serves as the primary income engine, anchoring the portfolio with reliable payouts, high return on equity, and steady earnings visibility.
As Southeast Asia’s largest bank, DBS continues to deliver strong profits, driven by its expanding wealth management franchise, where assets under management reached a new high of S$544 billion in 3Q2026.
DBS offers a strong baseline annual dividend backed by its 9M2026 performance, where net profit reached a record S$8.82 billion.
On top of its S$0.66 ordinary quarterly dividend, DBS currently pays a S$0.15 quarterly capital return dividend, although this is a time-limited programme rather than permanent income.
Supported by a 39% cost-income ratio and a strong Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio of 15.9%, DBS is well placed to keep producing steady cash flow even when broader equity markets trade sideways.
Singapore Exchange Limited (SGX: S68), or SGX — The Structural Growth Leader
Building long-term wealth requires capturing secular trends, and SGX Group sits right at the center of Asia’s financial engine.
As Singapore’s main stock exchange, SGX operates an enviable regulatory moat with multi-asset expansion across currencies, commodities, and cash equities.
In FY2026, net revenue surged 13.9% to S$1.478 billion while adjusted net profit, which excludes one-off items, jumped 24.6% to S$759.5 million.
Reported net profit rose 7.8% to S$698.4 million.
Growth is driven by surging multi-asset volumes. Foreign exchange (FX) headline average daily volume expanded 33.1% to US$190.2 billion, while Securities Daily Average Value (SDAV) leapt 34.9% to S$1.8 billion.
Supported by government liquidity initiatives and high capital efficiency, SGX raised its regular dividend to S$0.445 per share and proposed a one-off S$0.125 additional dividend.
That would take total FY2026 dividends to S$0.57 per share, up from S$0.375 in FY2025.
Backed by guided medium-term revenue growth of 6% to 8%, a position in SGX delivers a high-margin compounding engine designed to expand capital over time.
Sheng Siong Group Ltd (SGX: OV8) — The Defensive Blue Chip
When market turbulence strikes, defensive blue chips steady the portfolio ship, and Sheng Siong Group stands out as a prime example of operational resilience.
As one of Singapore’s leading grocery chains, with 96 stores across Singapore and Kunming, China, its business model is anchored to everyday essentials that generate sticky, predictable demand through all economic cycles.
In 1H2026, revenue surged 11.9% year on year (YoY) to S$855.4 million, while net profit rose 11.9% to S$81.0 million, propelled by four new store openings and an expanded gross profit margin of 31.8%.
What sets Sheng Siong apart is its bulletproof balance sheet: the group has no bank borrowings and held S$402.3 million in cash as at 30 June 2026.
This fortress cash position supports an increased interim dividend of S$0.0375 per share, up from S$0.0320 a year prior.
An allocation in Sheng Siong adds steady income and defensive qualities to the portfolio.
SATS Ltd (SGX: S51) — The Opportunity Play
Rounding out the four picks, SATS Ltd adds real upside potential through its post-acquisition operational recovery.
After acquiring Worldwide Flight Services, SATS became a global aviation services group, operating over 225 stations across 27 countries.
That scale is starting to pay off as global air cargo volumes keep growing.
In 1QFY2027, group revenue expanded 11.3% YoY to S$1.68 billion, while net profit rose 6% to S$75.1 million.
Growth was fuelled by a 12.8% surge in Gateway Services revenue to S$1.33 billion, as cargo volumes handled rose 8.6%, outpacing the global market benchmark.
While near-term geopolitical costs and fuel prices keep margins under pressure, SATS continues securing new contract wins with major airlines like
Singapore Airlines
(SGX: C6L) and Air France-KLM.
For investors, SATS offers long-term earnings upside as its cash flows strengthen.
What I Would Avoid
Capital preservation matters just as much as growth.
Don’t put all your money into one sector, or you’ll leave yourself wide open to sudden industry shocks.
Also, don’t just follow the
hottest stocks

title: Fed’s Logan favours at least two hikes, says pace could quicken
article:
(Nov 11): Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas president Lorie Logan said she still sees the need for at least two quarter-point rate increases, but that the pace of those hikes may need to be quicker than the Fed is moving this fall.

“It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases,” Logan said on Tuesday in prepared remarks for a conference in Houston, referring to the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on which she votes this year.

While the pace of hikes will depend on economic data and financial conditions, “It may be possible to move more rapidly this winter than the FOMC has moved so far this fall,” Logan added.

Fed officials left interest rates unchanged at their Oct 27-28 meeting after raising them by a quarter percentage point in September. That was the first rate hike since 2023 as policymakers seek to cool inflation that has been above their 2% target for more than five years.

A majority of officials in September signalled at least one more rate increase would be necessary this year, according to their median projection. While several Fed officials have reinforced this view in recent remarks and said hikes can come at a gradual pace, governor Christopher Waller earlier on Tuesday said the Fed should consider raising rates by a larger, half percentage point at its next meeting in December.

A report released on Tuesday morning showed the consumer price index rose by more than expected in October, with core inflation accelerating at a 0.3% pace from a month earlier. Logan said she’s concerned the Fed’s preferred gauge for inflation, due later this month, could show a similar pickup for October.

See also: US Treasuries drop as hot inflation backs December rate bets

title: IBM to end immigration sponsorship for roles in biggest unit
article:
(Nov 11): International Business Machines Corp (IBM) is ending immigration sponsorship for some roles in its largest division following a crackdown by the Trump administration on a visa programme that’s been a talent pipeline for the tech industry.

“We have opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles in IBM Consulting,” an IBM spokesperson said.

Impacted workers can continue working with IBM outside the US, or leave the company at the end of the year, according to a document shared with managers this week in that division seen by Bloomberg. Consulting is by far IBM’s largest division, with over 150,000 workers, according to its website.

The technology industry’s reliance on foreign workers has long been a flashpoint in the debate over immigration. Since President Donald Trump’s return to office last year, the administration has seized on those concerns and pressed tech giants to do more to train and hire US workers.

As part of that effort, Trump has moved to make it harder for companies to use H-1B visas to attract foreign talent. The changes have included proposals for US$100,000 filing fees for most candidates and tightening the rules of how the H-1B visas are awarded in an annual lottery, giving priority to companies offering the highest salaries.

See also: US stocks slide after hot inflation boosts December rate hike bets

Last month the administration accused Microsoft Corp, Adobe Inc and a half-dozen other companies of abusing a US worker visa programme and suspended them indefinitely from using it.

The affected IBM division participated “US high-skilled visa programmes” to address skill shortages, the spokesperson said. But participation has been declining for a number of years and skill availability and client need have evolved, the spokesperson said.

Big Blue has refashioned itself as a high-growth software company through major acquisitions of Red Hat, HashiCorp and Confluent. At the same time, its consulting business has lagged — the division’s growth has been largely flat since 2024.

title: US stocks slide after hot inflation boosts December rate hike bets
article:
(Nov 10): US equities are lower after hotter-than-expected inflation data released on Tuesday bolstered the case for an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve in December.

The S&P 500 index slid 0.6% as of 9.45am in New York, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 fell by as much as 1.3% before paring losses. Crude oil prices are continuing to retreat with the West Texas Intermediate oil prices falling to around US$85 a barrel.

Consumer prices excluding food and energy climbed 0.3% in October compared with a 0.2% estimate, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Investors “were hoping to see more relief off of the very elevated September reading,” said Vital Knowledge founder Adam Crisafulli.

The data is a “headwind” for risk assets as the market is now moving to price the possibility of the Fed raising rates by 50 basis points in December and more rate hikes beyond, “with higher front-end yields and a stronger dollar weighing on equity valuations,” said Jeff Schulze, head investment strategist at Franklin Templeton Institute.

Investors are also weighing news that Anthropic PBC is targeting US$1.4 trillion in fully diluted market value through its initial public offering (IPO). A handful of major chip names including Nvidia Corp, Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom Corp are looking to invest in the frontier artificial intelligence (AI) developer.

See also: Wall Street grapples with US$5.7 tril rout as AI bets unwind

Traders had already moved to fully price a quarter-point rate increase for December after governor Christopher Waller said earlier he supports a hike at that meeting, and didn’t rule out backing a half percentage point increase if inflation continues to accelerate. They extended those bets after the inflation data.

Inflation has been “relentless,” according to Aditya Bhave and Stephen Juneau, US economists at Bank of America. They warned that the Fed missing its 2% inflation mandate for a period that’s now pushing six years poses a risk to its credibility.

See also: Monster shares fall as weaker margins highlight cost burden

“It’s not just headline CPI that is too high, but the oil shock has seeped into core,” said Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management.

Cameron Dawson, chief investment officer at NewEdge Wealth, said in a Bloomberg TV interview that investor positioning has fallen to the 20th percentile and, as a result, “there’s room for a little bit of relief rally if sentiment improves even just slightly”.

Among single stock movers, Take-Two Interactive Software shares are rising after giving an outlook that Wall Street considers conservative ahead of the release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

title: Singapore wants to mobilise US$500 mil investment to build agri-food resilience
article:
Singapore has launched the SPIRE Asia Programme (Scaling Projects and Investments for Resilience in Asia) on Nov 10, which aims to mobilise investment to strengthen the climate resilience of Southeast Asia’s agri-food systems. SPIRE Asia seeks to mobilise up to US$500 ($640) million through a blended finance fund.

Jointly developed by the National Climate Change Secretariat (NCCS), Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and Enterprise Singapore (EnterpriseSG), SPIRE Asia seeks to address challenges hindering climate adaptation projects from being financed. These challenges include projects that are either too small or in premature stages of development or lack the data needed to meet investors’ requirements.

The blended finance fund, which will be overseen by MAS, will target agri-food companies and solutions that struggle to access financing on commercial terms, and help them scale climate-resilient practices. Details of the capital stack will be shared next year, says climate action ambassador Ravi Menon.

“The Singapore Government is prepared to contribute catalytic capital to the Fund, along with contributions from our international partners,” remarks Menon. “Interest from development finance institutions, multilateral banks, and commercial lenders has been encouraging.”

SPIRE Asia also includes the development of a data platform and market development facility. The former will bring together climate, agricultural and investment data to identify climate risks and adaptation opportunities, inform project development and investment decisions, and measure resilience outcomes.

Menon stresses that the data platform will build on existing data sets. He says: “We will not duplicate existing datasets. We will build on and connect them, translating data into insights for investors and project developers.”

See also: ACCA urges deeper CFO involvement in sustainability to enhance business resilience

He adds that the data platform, which is spearheaded by EnterpriseSG, will also help develop common approaches to measuring resilience outcomes.

Meanwhile, Temasek Trust will lead the market development facility, which seeks to develop promising agri-food adaptation opportunities into investment-ready projects. “The facility will coordinate relevant solutions, technical assistance, and project preparation,” shares Menon. “It will aggregate smaller projects into portfolios of sufficient scale, and connect them with investors, buyers, and implementation partners.”

title: Anthropic targets US$1.4 tril valuation in blockbuster IPO
article:
(Nov 10): Anthropic PBC is seeking a fully diluted valuation of about US$1.4 trillion ($1.8 trillion) in its initial public offering (IPO), in a bid to make history as the first frontier artificial intelligence (AI) lab to go public.

The Claude chatbot maker and some of its backers are seeking to raise as much as US$90.4 billion in the IPO and a private placement. The base offering would raise up to US$64.4 billion, with shares marketed for US$70 to US$78 each, according to a filing on Tuesday with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Anthropic is offering 801.4 million shares, while backers are selling 23.6 million shares.

The figure also includes a private placement set to raise US$26 billion in aggregate, to Advanced Micro Devices Inc, Broadcom Inc, Alphabet Inc’s Google, Micron Technology Inc, Microsoft Corp, Nvidia Corp and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, the filing showed.

At the top of the price range, Anthropic would have a market value of about US$1 trillion, based on the shares outstanding listed in the filing. Accounting for employee stock options, restricted shares and stock reserved for the company’s charitable donation matching programme, Anthropic would have a fully diluted value of about US$1.4 trillion.

Anthropic’s ambitious target, including the private placement, would hit roughly US$100 billion when including a so-called over-allotment option or greenshoe, Bloomberg News calculations showed. That would top SpaceX’s US$75 billion base offering, or the US$86.2 billion it raised with the greenshoe.

“Anthropic could justify a US$1.4 trillion market cap if annual recurring revenue reaches at least US$150 billion by 2027, supported by at least US$5 billion of new monthly ARR (annualised revenue run rate) after reporting US$81 billion in October,” wrote Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Mandeep Singh.

See also: Alibaba’s chip design unit T-Head files for listing in Hong Kong

The goal defies jitters from a sharp sell-off in AI-related stocks last week, driven by expectations that politicians promising tougher regulation of data centres and related infrastructure will drive up costs and limit development of the technology.

Investors are under pressure to decide whether valuations in AI reflect a plausible trajectory for a technology that many expect to transform the economy and society as a whole, or overconfidence in an investment theme that hasn’t yet proven its staying power.

“At a valuation of US$1.5 trillion, Anthropic would be worth about 11 times our 2027 revenue estimate and just seven times our 2028 estimate,” wrote William Blair analyst Arjun Bhatia. “This is an attractive multiple for a once-in-a-generation company like Anthropic operating in a technological shift that takes place once every few decades at best.”

See also: Anthropic IPO buyers see valuation as low as US$1.1 tril

The widespread adoption of Claude Code and rival tools by software developers point to the potential transformation of a wide range of professional activity, from discovering new miracle drugs to navigating complex legal and accounting rules to running a factory. Already, more than 90% of contributions to Anthropic’s code base were written by Claude, the filing showed.

Anthropic has introduced so-called vertical solutions in these areas, with particular emphasis on healthcare and life sciences. It counts Novartis AG chief executive officer Vas Narasimhan as one of its board members.

The company’s seven co-founders, including CEO Dario Amodei, are offering 3.38 million shares each in the IPO, the filing showed.

The IPO is set to price on Wednesday, Nov 18, and trade the following day, according to terms of the deal reviewed Bloomberg.

The company is planning a live-streamed event, at which Amodei will discuss the Claude chatbot maker’s IPO with JPMorgan Chase & Co CEO Jamie Dimon on Friday, Bloomberg News reported.

Sales are surging. The company reported a revenue run rate of US$81 billion as of Oct 31, up US$10 billion from the end of September, the filing showed. Anthropic had a US$65 billion run rate figure at the end of July, Bloomberg News reported. Anthropic defines the metric as annualising consumption-based fees for a trailing 28-day period and subscription-based fees for a single month.

Anthropic reported third-quarter revenue of nearly US$17 billion as of Sept 30, versus US$1.4 billion in the same period a year ago, its filing showed. On Monday, Anthropic unveiled new versions of its powerful Mythos and Fable models, both of which are faster than prior versions, while Fable is less expensive, as some companies cut back on their spending on the technology.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Keeping the pace of development running at a breakneck pace will require growing revenue faster than Anthropic’s spending on AI infrastructure. Anthropic has US$895 billion of commitments, most of which are for computing power, chips, the filing showed. About US$70 billion worth — a figure that’s larger than the individual market caps of roughly two-thirds of S&P 500 companies — are due just in the year through Sept 30, 2027.

Unlike other tech companies with sources of income such as advertising to fall back on, Anthropic will have to convince investors that its focus on AI alone will generate profit far beyond the technology’s surging costs. SpaceX may have tied its aspirations to AI when it pitched investors on its IPO, but most of its actual revenue at the time came from its other business lines.

That hasn’t stopped asset managers, venture capital firms and some of the biggest tech companies from backing Anthropic to the tune of tens of billions of dollars. Funds scattered across investment houses including Fidelity Investments, Capital Group and BlackRock Inc and venture capital firms such as Iconiq, Spark Capital and Sequoia Capital hold Anthropic shares before the IPO. Alphabet Inc’s Google, Amazon.com Inc and Microsoft Corp are backers as well as customers and key suppliers of computing power.

The speed of development has become increasingly controversial, with Anthropic’s own Amodei among those calling for top AI labs to “pace the frontier” in order to prioritise safety. Anthropic itself warned that the technology could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” in its IPO filing, if the technology isn’t developed with adequate safeguards and oversight.

Regulators, investors and even Anthropic’s employees have flagged the significant risk of humans losing control of the technology, with one putting the chance of AI eliminating all humans in the next decade at greater than 10%. Bill Gates said AI is powerful enough to drive events that cause “a billion deaths”.

Anthropic’s rival OpenAI is targeting a 2027 listing and CEO Sam Altman called 2026 an “ill-advised moment” for an IPO, citing concern over AI safety. The company is raising funds at a US$1.25 trillion valuation, people familiar with the matter have said.

Anthropic’s origin story centres around former OpenAI executives defecting because they wanted to prioritise AI safety. Nearly six years after its founding, Anthropic has structured itself as a public benefit corporation that balances shareholder interests with that of society, and whose governance includes a long-term benefit trust that has the power to elect and remove a majority of the members of the company’s board.

Anthropic’s seven co-founders hold roughly 1.4% stakes in the company, making them each billionaires several times over. That remains true even if they stick to their pledges to give 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropic causes.

The company’s total operating expenses jumped to US$17.5 billion in the third quarter, a 292% increase from a year prior. It flipped from an operating profit of US$974 million in the second quarter — its first after at least five quarters of operating losses — back to a negative US$567 million in the three months ended Sept 30, according to the filing.

The operating loss in the third quarter was primarily driven by US$5 billion of computing costs under short-term commitments and US$2 billion of non-cash charges related to the company’s charitable donation-matching programme.

AI pricing pressures have begun to hit Anthropic’s revenue. Lower prices on some of its new models, plus contractual discounts for some customers, reduced its revenue growth in the third quarter by about US$600 million, the filing showed.

Anthropic has cut prices in newer model roll-outs, including Opus 5.5 in September, and OpenAI has also introduced lower-priced models in recent months. The AI giants face growing competition from cheaper open-weight models, including from Chinese developers, which customers can download and fine-tune to their needs.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Morgan Stanley are leading Anthropic’s IPO, with participation from 20 other banks, the filing showed. The stock is expected to trade on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT.

title: US Treasuries drop as hot inflation backs December rate bets
article:
(Nov 10): Treasuries sank and traders solidified their bets that Federal Reserve officials will raise interest rates when they next meet in December after evidence of persistently hot US inflation.

The declines sent yields higher by more than 10 basis points (bps) for Treasuries maturing in two to five years on Tuesday after the economic data. Traders added to bets on at least two rate hikes by the middle of 2027 — and started to price in a small chance of a jumbo-sized half-point move in December.

Earlier, they’d fully priced in expectations for a quarter-point increase in December after Fed governor Christopher Waller said in London that he supported a rate increase and that he’d favour a half-point hike if inflation continued to accelerate.

“Clearly, the 50 basis point hike is on the table for discussion,” especially after Waller’s remarks, Tiffany Wilding, an economist at Pacific Investment Management Co, said on Bloomberg TV.

The consumer price index, excluding food and energy, rose 0.3% from a month earlier, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data. Overall prices climbed 0.4%. The BLS didn’t publish year-over-year changes because data collection was interrupted last October during the government shutdown. It follows a reading of the labour market last Friday that highlighted solid hiring trends and an unexpected jump in wage growth.

See also: US core CPI rises by more than forecast, supporting Fed hike

Traders saw both reports as supportive for higher US interest rates after policymakers opted for a quarter-point increase in September and then left rates steady in October. The 10-year note was 5bps higher at 4.94% ahead of the Treasury’s auction of a US$42 billion new issue at 1pm New York time.

“The Fed skipped October and now will probably need to do some make up,” Alex Pelle, senior US economist at Mizuho, said. The “debate will likely be between 25 versus 50 basis points at the December meeting, not zero versus 25.”

US government bonds have recovered some of the year’s losses tied to concerns that the war in Iran and elevated energy costs would keep inflation sticky. After registering multi-decade peaks in early October, the market has benefitted from its reputation as a haven. A Democratic sweep in the midterm elections intensified angst around the sustainability of spending on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, leading to a selloff in the stock market and a dash for safety.

See also: US small-business plans to raise prices reach four-year high

“The AI tech trade has to settle down, and once that happens, you can make a very strong case that this plunge in yields by 50 basis points over the past month was really just safe haven demand,” said Kevin Flanagan, head of investment strategy at WisdomTree. “If you look at what has occurred in terms of the economic data, it would suggest that we could see yields rise — and perhaps back to 5% for the 10-year.”

title: Delfi’s 3QFY2026 net sales drop 5.5% y-o-y due to weaker rupiah
article:
Confectioner Delfi saw its net sales dropped y-o-y by 5.5% to US$118 ($151) million for 3QFY2026 ended Sept 30. Gross profit margin declined by 220 basis points y-o-y to 23.2% while ebitda remained steady at US$10.2 million.

On a constant currency basis, there would be no decline in net sales and ebitda would have been 10% higher for the quarter.

For the first nine months of the year, net sales rose y-o-y by 0.1% to US$384.6 million, with weaker gross margin of 24.9%, compared to the 26.8% of the previous corresponding period. Ebitda would also go down to US$33.6 million, 2.6% less y-o-y. On a constant currency basis, net sales would have increased 1.9% y-o-y and ebitda by 2.6% y-o-y.

Delfi’s key market of Indonesia saw weaker performance for the quarter and the nine months, mainly due to the weaker Indonesian rupiah. Meanwhile, its regional markets saw softer sales for 3Q but grew overall for the nine months.

Besides the weaker rupiah, sustained higher raw material costs are impacting Delfi’s performance.

As at Sept 30, Delfi held cash of around US$55.5 million, down from the US$68 million it held on Dec 31, 2025. Bank borrowings increased by US$7.2 million to US$21.8 million.

See also: Addvalue Technologies reports 114% y-o-y earnings jump to US$4.23 mil for 1HFY2027

The firm generated US$13.1 million in net cash from operating activities for the nine months while allocating US$5.8 million for capex.

Moving forward into 2027, Delfi expects the global operating environment to remain uncertain. With cocoa prices remaining elevated by historical standards, despite easing from record highs. Intensifying geopolitical pressures in the Middle East continue to drive volatility in energy costs, supply chains, and global currencies, while recent economic uncertainty and higher inflation in Indonesia could dampen consumer demand, it notes.

Shares in Delfi rose by 0.5 cents or 0.7% to 69 cents on Nov 10.

title: Addvalue Technologies reports 114% y-o-y earnings jump to US$4.23 mil for 1HFY2027

title: Alibaba’s chip design unit T-Head files for listing in Hong Kong
article:
(Nov 10): Alibaba Group Holding Ltd’s in-house chip design unit T-Head has filed for a Hong Kong listing, moving ahead with a proposed spin-off of a business that supplies data-centre processors in China.

The Hong Kong stock exchange has cleared Alibaba to proceed with the move and T-Head submitted its listing application on Sept 11, Alibaba said in an exchange filing on Tuesday. The size and structure of the offering haven’t been finalised.

T-Head, wholly owned by Alibaba, is a provider of full-stack data-centre chips that enable system-level computing solutions in China, according to the filing. It is expected to remain a subsidiary of Alibaba after the listing.

Alibaba said the spin-off would allow investors to value T-Head separately from the rest of the group and could attract investors seeking dedicated exposure to the chip business. A separate listing would also give T-Head direct access to equity and debt capital markets and enhance its ability to secure bank financing, according to the filing.

title: UMS doubles patmi y-o-y for 3QFY2026
article:

Segmentally, revenue for the semiconductor business grew 65% to $83.1 million for the quarter; aerospace flew up 55% y-o-y to $9.75 million; and the others segment saw revenue grew by 2% to $2.54 million.

The revenue surge in the semiconductor segment was driven mainly by strong sales in both semiconductor integrated system sales as well as component sales, says UMS.

Compared to the previous quarter, semiconductor segment sales grew 10%. This is mainly attributable to higher component sales to the new major customer, partially offset by a decline in the Integrated System sales as a result of shortage of OEM parts. These shortages are expected to ease in the months ahead.

Geographically, the firm’s key markets performed better y-o-y in the third quarter, reporting double-digit growth with Malaysia as the standout that recorded a 209% surge in sales as the production ramp up of semiconductor components for UMS’s new major customer accelerated.

On a sequential basis, sales improved in all key markets, except for Singapore which fell 16% q-o-q to $44.9 million.

The 3Q results bring nine months earnings to $54.5 million, representing a 78% y-o-y increase. Revenue for the nine months rose 37% to nearly $252 million. The semiconductor unit reported a 38% y-o-y increase in revenue to $217.5 million for 9MFY2026; aerospace experienced a 43% y-o-y revenue increase to $25.6 million; and revenue for the others segment increased by 3% y-o-y to $8.8 million.

UMS delivered a “standout” performance, says UMS CEO Andy Luong. He adds: “Despite unprecedented uncertainties brought about by US trade tariffs, intensifying geopolitical tensions, rising inflation and supply chain constraints, the group persisted in our strategic expansion plans to strengthen our production capabilities and facilities, enabling us to meet the strong ramp-up of orders from our major customers. Our focus on operational execution has paid off — helping us deliver the Group's record revenue performance in the past three financial years.”

Besides highlighting the “bright” outlook for the semiconductor industry, UMS says that its key customers’ forecasts are expected to exceed industry estimates. “The Group’s existing major customer has projected strong multi-year growth driven by artificial intelligence compute demand, data centre expansion and advanced chip architectures,” UMS notes. “The Group’s new key customer has also issued very upbeat guidance, citing elevated demand driven by artificial intelligence and increased chip complexity which will propel the company to generate record quarterly revenue and profitability.”

UMS says that it has taken “decisive” measures to capture the “multitude” of growth opportunities ahead.
