title: Macron in talks with Gulf countries about providing insurance for Hormuz transit — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 10): French President Emmanuel Macron is negotiating with Gulf countries to find a way to lower insurance costs for vessels going through the strait of Hormuz, where transport has been disrupted since the US and Israel began strikes on Iran in February.

Discussions are ongoing with Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states to design a publicly backed vehicle that would assume parts of the insurance risk for vessels to go through the waterway and facilitate deliveries of energy by lowering shipment costs, according to people familiar with the matter.

The discussions involve different French ministries, from energy to foreign affairs and finance, said two of the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

It’s not immediately clear how such an insurance scheme would work in practice and what guarantees can be given. US President Donald Trump had announced a US$20 billion reinsurance programme for oil tankers earlier this year, but insurance costs have remained exorbitant as a result of repeated Iranian attacks on shipping.

A spokesman for the French president’s office confirmed that work was ongoing.

Macron traveled to Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia last month to secure commitments to supply France with more diesel in coming months, in a bid to lower fuel costs that are contributing to social unrest in France. Macron also secured liquefied natural gas from Qatar for the winter months, which represents roughly 7% of the nation’s average monthly gas use.

Yet getting the fuel to French consumers from Qatar may prove considerably harder than securing it on paper. The Strait of Hormuz, the main route for the supply, remains heavily disrupted because of the US-Iran war, with gas volumes way below normal. Oil and gas prices have surged in Europe in recent months as attacks on vessels around the strait curbed shipments and boosted insurance costs.

Pump prices surged across the world after the US and Israel launched military strikes on Iran in February, disrupting exports of crude and reined products through the crucial Strait of Hormuz. Trump even conceded that Republicans lost the midterm elections because of the war in the Middle East, which has also driven up costs of insuring the ships going through.

title: Sea misses earnings estimates on rising AI costs
article:
(Nov 10): Sea Ltd earnings missed estimates after the Southeast Asia e-commerce leader boosted spending in artificial intelligence (AI) features and intense competition weighed on prices.

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation for the three months through September climbed 29% to US$931 million ($1.19 billion), the company said on Tuesday. Analysts estimated US$990 million on average, according to Bloomberg-compiled data. Revenue rose 43% to US$8.6 billion, exceeding predictions. The stock fell more than 10% in pre-market trading before paring some losses.

Battle for customers with ByteDance Ltd’s TikTok Shop, Alibaba Group Holding Ltd’s Lazada and recently listed Shein Global Holdings Ltd is weighing on prices at Sea’s e-commerce arm Shopee, its biggest unit. At the same time, its expenditures are increasing as the company embeds AI features into its product offerings and works to expand in areas such as cloud computing and food delivery.

Through Monday, Sea’s shares had plunged about 40% from the start of the year, weighed down by rising oil prices and fierce competition. Chief executive officer Forrest Li’s plan to begin offering cloud services to global firms sent the stock lower in October as analysts flagged the firm was unclear about how it would build the new business and how much it would spend.

The AI-led expansion would set Sea against the likes of deep-pocketed cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services. Yet it’s unlikely that Sea could operate at the same scale as its more established rivals, as the firm would need to spend substantially on resources like chips and storage before turning a profit, said Bloomberg Intelligence analysts including Lea El-Hage.

See also: SoftBank loses US$7 bil in one quarter after big US data centre write-down

At the same time, Sea is eyeing a public listing of its financial services arm Monee. The potential spin-off would give Monee independent access to capital while its margins stay fragile, according to El-Hage.

Those moves come as the firm seeks to carve out space beyond its home ground — expanding its Shopee retail empire to Brazil, while grappling with possible regulatory hurdles in major regional market Indonesia. Adjusted Ebitda at Shopee rose 45% to US$269.2 million in the latest quarter, while sales jumped 41% to US$6.1 billion.

The company said its board authorised additional US$1 billion in stock buy-backs, after the company purchased a similar amount under a previous repurchase programme.

title: US small-business plans to raise prices reach four-year high
article:
(Nov 10): More than a third of US small-business owners plan to increase prices in the coming months, the most in more than four years, pointing to persistent inflationary headwinds.

The net share of firms who plan to raise prices in the next three months climbed to 37% in October, according to data from the National Federation of Independent Business (NFIB) released on Tuesday. The small-business optimism index was little changed at 97.8.

The group’s uncertainty index, while still elevated, matched the lowest level of President Donald Trump’s second term. And more firms reported the health of their business as either good or excellent.

“There was little change in optimism among small businesses in October as owners navigated enduring challenges, though there were some encouraging developments,” NFIB chief economist Bill Dunkelberg said in a statement. “Even with inflation pressures continuing to strain operations, more Main Street owners reported their businesses in good or excellent health, and actual sales improved.”

While firms continued to note labour quality or availability as the single most important problem, 21% of small-business owners ranked taxes as the top issue. That was the highest since May 2021 and up 10 points from September. About 17% of firms pointed to inflation as heightened input costs continued to burden small businesses.

See also: Fed’s Waller backs rate hike in December, says open to larger move

title: SoftBank loses US$7 bil in one quarter after big US data centre write-down
article:
(Nov 10): SoftBank Group Corp reported its first net loss in almost two years after the tech investor swallowed a US$3.7 billion ($4.7 billion) write-down over its US data-centre projects and artificial intelligence (AI) valuations dipped around the world.

The company swung to a ¥1.12 trillion (US$7.1 billion or $9.1 billion) loss in its fiscal second quarter after writing down non-refundable advance payments it made to secure power-generation equipment for its eight-gigawatt Ohio project and other US data centres. Analysts on average expected a profit of ¥129 billion from the OpenAI backer.

The loss points to the tension at the heart of founder Masayoshi Son’s race to build the infrastructure needed to support AI development even as the costs of both hardware and financing rise. The write-down suggests the company may be rethinking how quickly and how far in advance it commits billions of dollars to that build-out.

SoftBank had previously hurried to secure the equipment it needs for AI data centres, chief financial officer Yoshimitsu Goto said during an earnings conference on Tuesday. While there’s no plan to downsize the Ohio data-centre project, the company’s conducting “a thorough reassessment” including a review of its procurement strategy, he said. Goto did not go into specifics about the cause of the write-downs.

SoftBank’s shift in procurement strategy follows a sharp revision in the global AI outlook after the victory of Democratic candidates who ran on anti-data-centre platforms during the US midterm elections. That’s exacerbated fears about rising debt levels and questions about the sustainability of AI spending.

See also: Sea misses earnings estimates on rising AI costs

“We need to watch closely” the impact of the US midterm elections on AI sentiment, Goto said.

Son has directed billions of dollars into AI-related hardware and applications, including almost US$65 billion in OpenAI and a US$3.1 billion acquisition of data-centre operator DigitalBridge Group Inc. The spending has fuelled investor concerns over SoftBank’s growing reliance on debt to finance its AI ambitions.

See also: Australia to create AI safety regulator, mandatory safety rules

Rising financing costs are already hurting SoftBank. Group-wide interest expenses for the six months to September more than doubled from a year ago to ¥676 billion.

“We can treat the loss from the review of the AI data centre plans as temporary. The more worrying factor is the increase in financial costs,” said Kazuki Sawamura, a strategist at Shinkin Asset Management. “If investment income and the value of its holdings don’t grow steadily from here, the interest burden could squeeze earnings and heighten concern about SoftBank’s financial health.”

In the September quarter, declines in the stock prices of chipmakers Arm Holdings plc and Intel Corp, as well as South Korean e-commerce giant Coupang Inc, further dragged down SoftBank’s bottom line.

The Vision Fund segment, which oversees stakes in hundreds of tech start-ups, logged a loss of ¥81.6 billion, compared with market expectations for a profit. The unit booked a quarterly investment gain of ¥85.4 billion, helped by higher valuations at ByteDance Ltd and Lenskart Solutions Ltd.

SoftBank’s own shares have plunged more than 50% from their record high in June, and volatility in its stock price has been high as investors try to gauge the risks and opportunities around its AI investments. Its stock price is down 12% from the start of the year.

That’s as potential investors weigh a valuation as low as US$1.1 trillion for Anthropic PBC, down from a previously touted figure of US$2 trillion, people familiar with the matter said. Earlier, OpenAI raised about US$11 billion at a US$1.25 trillion valuation, after initially seeking US$30 billion at a US$1.4 trillion value, Bloomberg News reported.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Son’s reliance on debt markets has made SoftBank’s bonds especially sensitive and has lifted its credit default swaps to their highest in years. The company’s loan-to-value ratio stood at 15.9% at the end of September, well below the 25% threshold it’s set to ensure financial stability, Goto said.

SoftBank prepaid US$30 billion of a US$40 billion bridge facility agreement by securing a new term loan and by raising US$7.35 billion via prepaid forward contracts backed by its Intel stake and by raising another US$5 billion through a margin loan backed by Arm shares.

title: French grocer Casino agrees to debt deal with opposing creditors
article:
(Nov 10): French supermarket chain Casino Guichard-Perrachon SA has reached an agreement on restructuring its debt, after facing opposition from a group of lenders to its initial plan.

 

A vehicle ultimately controlled by Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky will remain in control under the deal, according to a presentation from the grocery chain, which is set to be re-named Plesio. The plan envisages converting a similar amount of the €1.4 billion term loan into equity as under the previous plan, but now stipulates that Kretinsky’s vehicle will repurchase the newly-converted shares, allowing creditors to recover more value.

The newly-hatched deal comes after a group of investors holding around 90% of the term loans mounted a series of challenges to the original plan under a French restructuring process known as accelerated safeguard. Upon finalisation of the new deal, the creditor group will withdraw its opposition, which included seeking the termination of the existing plans.

A number of aggressive restructuring plans in Europe have recently been challenged by creditors who consider themselves short-changed in plans put together by companies. Bondholders of Grupo Antolin-Irausa, for example, have been negotiating with the Spanish auto-parts manufacturer after they sought to thwart a deal that disadvantaged them.

The Casino case also demonstrates the limits of overly debtor-friendly plans. Creditors had presented their own proposal which demonstrated their willingness to take over the business before the company filed for accelerated safeguard. However, the grocery chain ultimately backed a deal which saw Kretinsky’s vehicle stay in place. The latest plan represents a compromise.

The company is aiming to have the approval of the amended safeguard plans by mid-February 2027 and to close the restructuring in March. Following the restructuring, existing shareholders of publicly-traded Casino will retain less than 0.1% of the firm’s capital. Casino’s market capitalisation is around €64.2 million, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

See also: Commerzbank flags deposit competition before UniCredit deal
• Around €390 million of new cash equity will be injected by France Retail Holdings (FRH), Kretinsky’s vehicle
• Conversion into equity of around €610 million of existing term loan and up to €110 million of existing revolving-credit facility amount
• Reinstatement of €800 million of term loan principal amount for five-year term
• A sale of the shares held by term loan creditors to FRH will be completed immediately following the closing of the restructuring
• FRH purchase of shares to be funded by a vendor loan granted by term loan lenders that opt to sell their shares
• Term loan lenders also have the option to seek enhanced reinstatement of their claim instead of selling shares to FRH, however the loan lender group, the TLB Steerco, has agreed to sell the shares

title: Link REIT to acquire 50.1% of Eastpoint Mall from Income Insurance
article:
On Nov 10, Link, the manager of Link REIT, and Income Insurance announced that Link REIT will acquire a 50.1% interest in the mall from Income Insurance for $239.5 million. Income Insurance will retain the remaining 49.9% interest. Link will serve as Eastpoint Mall’s asset manager and property manager.

Link will work closely with Income Insurance, as advised by CapitaLand Investment (CLI), to execute the transaction and develop an asset enhancement strategy, unlocking the value-creation potential of Eastpoint Mall.

For Income Insurance, the transaction represents a considered and strategic decision to optimise its property portfolio in line with its core return objectives and long-term sustainability goals. Pursuant to the advice of its real estate investment manager, CLI, appointed in April 2026, the transaction enables Income Insurance to re-cycle capital to work where it can best serve policyholders over the long term.

John Saunders, Link’s Executive Director and Chief Investment Officer, said: “We are primarily focused on the divestment of non-core assets, however, this is a compelling and capital efficient investment which underscores Link’s focus on its core strengths in owning and actively managing retail assets across Asia Pacific.”

Ellina Chia, Link’s Head of Singapore Regional Centre, said: “We are delighted to be partnering with Income Insurance and further growing our retail asset management business. We see opportunities to unlock further value through active asset management and targeted asset enhancement initiatives which will strengthen Eastpoint Mall’s positioning and relevance within the local community.”

David Chua, Chief Investment Officer, Income Insurance, said: “Eastpoint Mall has long served as an important retail and community landmark in the eastern part of Singapore and Income is pleased to continue our interests in its next phase of growth. Through our retained significant stake, we will collaborate with Link to support the rejuvenation of Eastpoint Mall and its surrounding community. This reflects our focus on creating long-term value for our policyholders while continuing to serve our customers and Singaporeans.”

See also: Starhill Global REIT’s anchor tenant at David Jones Building enters voluntary administration, potential DPU impact

Upon completion of the transaction, which is expected to take place in the first quarter of 2027, Link and Income Insurance will work together to ensure a smooth transition of the mall’s asset management and operations. The partners will also undertake a phased asset enhancement initiative (AEI), with works expected to commence in 2027. During the AEI, Eastpoint Mall will remain open and continue to serve the community.

Following the completion of the transaction, Link will manage three retail assets in Singapore, namely Eastpoint Mall, Jurong Point, and AMK Hub.

Directly connected to Simei MRT station, Eastpoint Mall is a suburban retail property in eastern Singapore, with approximately 214,000 square feet of net lettable area.

Link will fund the acquisition through internal resources and debt facilities.

title: GIC, Macquarie said to mull options for Philippines' EDC, including stake sale
article:
(Nov 10): Macquarie Group Ltd’s asset management arm and Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC Pte Ltd are exploring options for their stake in Energy Development Corp (EDC), including a possible sale, people familiar with the matter said.

Macquarie Asset Management and GIC, which jointly hold about a third of the Philippine geothermal energy company, have brought in Goldman Sachs Group Inc to help with the review, according to the people, who asked not to be identified because the information is private.

Other infrastructure-focused funds and industry players have shown early interest in the stake, which could be valued at about US$2 billion ($2.55 billion), the people said. Considerations are preliminary and may not lead to a deal, they added.

Representatives of EDC, GIC, Goldman Sachs and Macquarie declined to comment.

A Macquarie fund and an affiliate of GIC bought the EDC stake for about US$1.3 billion in 2017. Following EDC’s delisting from the Philippine Stock Exchange a year later, the buying consortium holds a 54% economic interest in the company. It holds about a third of the voting shares.

In July this year, Indonesia’s PT Barito Renewables Energy made an unsolicited, non-binding offer to buy EDC for about US$5 billion — a big deal for Asia’s clean energy sector. EDC backer First Gen Corp confirmed that it had received the offer, but hadn’t engaged in discussions.

See also: Energy security needs action on electrification — International Renewable Energy Agency

Philippines-based First Gen, controlled by the prominent Lopez family, has assets in areas such as geothermal, hydropower, wind, solar and natural gas. KKR & Co sold its US$410 million stake and exited First Gen in September after its bid to take the company private at 35 pesos (US$0.55 or $0.71) a share was rejected.

First Gen’s shares rose 1.5% on Tuesday to 19.80 pesos, having hit a high of 31.85 pesos in mid-August around KKR’s offer.

title: Emperador 3Q earnings rise 47% y-o-y
article:
For 3QFY2026 ended Sept 30, Mainboard-listed Emperador Inc has reported net profit attributable to owners of 1.08 billion Philippine pesos ($21.9 million), up 47% y-o-y.Revenue topped 17.4 billion Philippine pesos, up nearly 34% y-o-y.

Total earnings for the first nine months reached 4.79 billion Philippine pesos, up 2.3% y-o-y, while revenue increased by 14% y-o-y to $41 billion Philippine pesos.

Both the brandy and scotch whisky segments saw growth, according to Emperador.

Shares in the counter closed flat at 31 cents on Nov 10.

title: China chip supplier Xinde jumps in HK debut as Denglin slumps
article:
(Nov 10): Jiangsu Xinde Semiconductor Technology Co’s shares surged in their Hong Kong debut while Suzhou Denglin Technology Co’s stock slumped on their first day after the Chinese chip suppliers raised a combined US$301 million in their initial public offerings, entering the market at a time of extreme volatility, especially for technology stocks.

Chip assembly and testing company Xinde Semi’s shares rose 28.3% Tuesday (Nov 10) after the company priced 106.6 million shares at HK$8.88 each, below the maximum, to raise HK$946 million. Meanwhile, Denglin’s shares fell as 7.8% after the graphics processing unit maker priced 6.1 million shares at HK$231 apiece, the low end of the marketed range, to raise HK$1.41 billion.

Technology stocks have been through bouts of volatility recently, buffeted by doubts over the artificial intelligence buildout and the impact of the US midterm election. On Monday, Asian equity markets rebounded after last week’s steep declines, even after Nvidia Corp's board revealed an investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted in a foreign espionage plot.

The debuts are an important bellwether for new listings in Hong Kong. First-time share sales in the city have raised US$51.9 billion this year, approaching the 2010 record of US$57.8 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg, largely driven by Chinese technology companies. But the flow has started to slow as issuers and investors grow increasingly cautious, with the AI trade wobbling and regulators intensifying scrutiny of deals.

In a sign of the resilience of investor demand, RelyEZ Energy Storage Technology Co shares soared as much as 129% after the Chinese energy storage system provider raised HK$562.7 million, with the retail tranche 1,389 times subscribed.

See also: TSMC’s revenue rises 60% in a sign of resilient AI chip demand

Successful debuts could pave the way for a busy year-end after only three IPOs were completed in October, versus an average of about 13 a month from January through September, data compiled by Bloomberg show.

title: Canada looking at relief from US tariff after Trump’s midterm election loss
article:
(Nov 10): Canada will seek to ease trade frictions with the US after tariff-weary voters rebuked US President Donald Trump in midterm elections, Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand said.

Canada’s industries have been hit hard by the US president’s trade wars, Anand said on Bloomberg Television. That has prompted Canada to strike back and find alternative trade partners, she said. But America’s changing political mood has created an opening for detente.

“We’re talking about just a week or so out of these elections, and Canada very much hopes that we will have progress on the trade front,” she said, citing tariffs on lumber, steel, aluminium and automobiles. “These sectors are being hit very hard in Canada with workers losing their jobs.”

Anand was in Paris to attend a meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) foreign ministers, including US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

Canada has signed more than 20 security, economic and defence agreements over the past year, she said, making it the only G7 nation to have a free trade agreement with each member of the group of advanced economies.

“This is the work that we are doing to double non-US trade over the next 10 years,” she said.

Anand said she also recently visited the United Arab Emirates, which is hosting Russian and Ukraine officials this week to discuss Moscow’s ongoing war. The foreign minister said the talks will focus on future security guarantees for Kyiv, including for energy infrastructure and agriculture products leaving Ukrainian ports.

She said Canada plans to sign a 100-year agreement with Ukraine this year focused on drone production and troop training.

Canada and the European Union are also tightening cooperation across several strategic areas including critical minerals, energy, artificial intelligence, technology and cloud computing, she said.

title: Yangzijiang Shipbuilding’s order-wins exceed target by 55%
article:
Mainboard-listed Yangzijiang (YZJ) Shipbuilding has announced a strong year for orderbook wins in its 3QFY2026 business update.

At the ten-month mark, the company has secured US$6.98 ($8.92) billion in year-to-date order wins. This is 55% higher than its FY2026 target of US$4.5 billion. In total, YZJ Shipbuilding’s orderbook stood at US$26.3 billion as at Oct 31, with deliveries slated up to 2030.

Around two-third of its orderbook value comprises clean energy newbuild vessels. YZJ Shipbuilding executive chairman Ren Letian says that the company made “strong” progress in securing new orders. “This was underpinned by contracts for ultra-large LNG dual-fuel containerships and large bulk carriers,” he adds.

Ren expects newbuild demand to remain “firm”, supported by fleet renewal, the transition towards dual-fuel vessels and ongoing trade route disruptions that continue to absorb shipping capacity.

“With delivery slots across the industry largely committed through 2029, we remain selective, prioritising vessel types and contract terms that preserve the quality of our orderbook,” he remarks. “Looking ahead, our focus is on executing our orderbook with quality, ramping up our Hongyuan yard to support growth in the coming years, and progressively filling our remaining 2030 delivery slots, while delivering sustainable returns to shareholders.”

Shares in YZJ Shipbuilding rose 5.5% or 24 cents on Nov 10, closing at $4.59.

title: Hong Kong listing proceeds hit six-year high, close to record
article:
(Nov 10): Hong Kong listing proceeds have climbed to the highest in six years after a fresh wave of offerings helped the market regain some of the momentum it had lost in recent months.

First-time share sales have raised US$51.9 billion ($66.3 billion) this year, rising past the 2020 mark of US$51.6 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. That makes 2026 the second-best year ever, with the 2010 record of US$57.8 billion still in sight.

Highlighting the breadth of fundraising, 10 deals surpassed US$1 billion in proceeds this year, including Zhongji Innolight Co’s US$7.8 billion listing in July and Luxshare Precision Industry Co’s US$3.2 billion offering in June. That compares with seven such transactions in 2010, when AIA Group Ltd’s US$20.4 billion listing, the largest in the city’s history, accounted for more than a third of the year’s proceeds.

The deal flow this year has been dominated by Chinese companies in the artificial intelligence (AI) supply chain raising funds to keep up with demand and compete with rivals mostly in the US, where marquee listings also drove one of the best initial public offering (IPO) years ever. But the pace has slowed as investors have become more cautious about the AI trade. About one in four deals in 2026 has failed to reach completion, the highest rate of abandoned listings since the global financial crisis.

“It’s fitting that this boom in new issues has centred on the US and China,” said Phillip Wool, the head of portfolio management at Rayliant Global Advisors. “These are markets with investors whose appetite for AI-related stocks and capital to deploy in the space has been extremely strong. It’s clear that we are at something of a decision point for AI investors, who have been funding all of that equity issuance.”

See also: New World’s top shareholder seeks bank loan as equity deal looms — Bloomberg

While the market has slowed, bankers say several sizeable deals have simply been pushed back and are filling next year’s pipeline. Baidu Inc’s AI chip unit Kunlunxin, which filed confidentially in January for a US$2 billion IPO in Hong Kong, may now list in 2027 rather than this year, people with knowledge of the matter have said. Alibaba Group Holding Ltd is preparing to list its chipmaking arm T-Head as well.

“The pipeline itself isn’t the constraint; investor demand and pricing are,” said Bush Chu, the investment director of Chinese equities at Aberdeen Investments. “Into next year, we don’t expect the pipeline to dry up. The applicant queue remains deep and some large deals deferred this year could land in 2027.”

A number of companies await approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission and issuers try to time launches in choppy markets. The Hang Seng Index has shed 4.5% this year on concerns over rising tech financing costs and a slow recovery in China.

See also: Hong Kong bourse operator's profit falls as AI scrutiny hits listings, trading

This month is already busier as chip supplier Suzhou Denglin Technology Co and chip packaging and testing company Jiangsu Xinde Semiconductor Technology Co began trading on Tuesday. With several more deals in the market, the flow is picking up from October, when only three listings were completed, versus an average of about 13 a month from January through September, data compiled by Bloomberg showed.

title: Fed’s Waller backs rate hike in December, says open to larger move
article:
(Nov 10): Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller on Tuesday said he supports an interest-rate hike in December, and warned that if inflation continues to accelerate he would support a half-percentage-point increase to protect the central bank’s credibility.

The blunt outlook from Waller is the strongest argument yet from a Fed official that policymakers not only need to raise rates in December, but may need to do so by more than the quarter point that markets expect.

Describing the economy as strong and the labour market as stable, Waller said inflation remains too high. He then hinged his policy prescription on consumer price inflation data for October that the Bureau of Labor Statistics will release later on Tuesday morning.

“If, as I expect, the monthly rate of inflation improves in October, I am leaning towards supporting an increase in our policy rate of 25 basis points,” Waller said in a speech in London.

“But if the October CPI [consumer price index] inflation data out later today are similar to the past two monthly readings — with core CPI inflation around 0.3% or even higher — then a stronger policy move may be needed,” he said. “In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting.”

Under that scenario, Waller added, moving rates by the conventional quarter point would do little to win confidence that the Fed is tackling inflation.

See also: US consumer sentiment unexpectedly rises, fuelled by independents

“Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take,” he said.

Fed officials held interest rates steady last month, saying the “accumulation of more information” would allow them to determine the best level for policy. The 10-2 decision to stay put followed a unanimous move to lift the benchmark rate in September by a quarter percentage point to a target range of 3.75% to 4%.

Several policymakers speaking since the meeting have touted the need for additional rate hikes, and traders on Monday saw about an 85% chance of an increase in December.

See also: US adds 165,000 jobs, topping all forecasts in broad advance

Data last week showed jobs growth surged in October and the unemployment rate edged lower. Fed officials will receive one more jobs report and a full slate of inflation data — beginning with the consumer price index for October — before they gather again in December.

title: Brits snap up hand sanitiser, canned food on stockpile advice
article:
(Nov 10): Sales of hand sanitiser, bottled water and canned food soared after the UK government urged households to stockpile for potential disruptions.

Shoppers responded quickly to the “Be Ready” campaign last month, according to data from retail tracker Worldpanel by Numerator published Tuesday (Nov 10). In the 10 days after the advice was posted Oct 22, sales of hand sanitiser jumped 83% from a year earlier, with bottled water up 67% and canned goods 37%.

The UK government wants households to keep enough supplies to be self-sufficient for three days in the event of a national emergency, including non-perishable food, water, flashlights and batteries.

“Shoppers clearly took notice of the ‘Be Ready’ campaign, but this wasn’t panic buying,” said Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel, adding that shoppers were adding items from the government advice to their weekly shop rather than “piling their trolleys high".

The number of people buying tinned meat each day after the campaign launch rose 43%, Worldpanel said, equivalent to an extra 400,000 shoppers a day.

Food and drink manufacturer Princes Group plc, whose products include Branston baked beans and Napolina canned tomatoes, reported Tuesday an increase in demand following the government’s campaign launch.

See also: Bank of England may raise high-risk mortgage threshold, FT says

Overall grocery inflation ticked higher to 2.6% in the four weeks ending Nov 1, though that was still slower than the UK’s overall inflation rate.

title: Thailand sets 70dB noise, heat limits for data centres
article:
(Nov 10): Thailand imposed new noise, heat and water rules on data centres, putting specific environmental limits on an industry expanding rapidly with the artificial intelligence investment boom.

Noise must be kept around 70 A-weighted decibels, or dBA, a measure adjusted to reflect how humans perceive sound, when uninterrupted power-supply systems are running, Danucha Pichayanan, secretary-general of Thailand’s economic planning agency, said Tuesday (Nov 10) after the cabinet approved the regulations.

Temperature increases at the boundary of a data centre site will be limited to one or two degrees Celsius, and cooling water must be recirculated and discharged water tested, he said. Facilities in industrial estates will face additional requirements.

The rules are part of Thailand’s effort to capture the economic benefits of surging investment in computing infrastructure without overwhelming water and power supplies or creating problems for surrounding communities.

“We will implement the highest standards,” Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas said. Projects that fail to meet security and environmental requirements “will not be allowed to proceed".

Thailand attracted more than US$50 billion of investment-promotion applications in the first nine months of the year, with AI-related projects accounting for about 70% of their value, according to the Board of Investment.

See also: Tokyo is world’s priciest city to construct data centres; Singapore ranks fourth: report

title: Energy security needs action on electrification — International Renewable Energy Agency
article:
(Nov 10): Wars and energy shocks are accelerating the case to electrify economies as governments seek to curb exposure to volatile fossil-fuel prices and limit imports.

Electricity is increasingly replacing fossil fuels in transport, heating and industry, and nations should aim to accelerate that shift, Francesco La Camera, director general of the International Renewable Energy Agency, said at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey.

A flagship ambition for the talks is to win commitments to increase electricity’s share of global final energy consumption from just over 20% today to 35% by 2035.

That is “exactly what we have to put into action to keep our promise alive,” La Camera said in an interview Monday. “If we don’t act, we cannot win the challenge of climate change.”

Electrification can reduce reliance on imported fuels, stabilise energy costs and strengthen economic resilience, La Camera said. “Everyone has realised that a centralised system based on fossil fuels is not good for energy security,” he said.

A series of meetings at the summit Tuesday were convening energy ministers, bankers and company executives on the electrification goal.

See also: China set to lead world in energy investment in 2026, CCTV says

“If you succeed in electrification, you’ll reduce dependency and you’ll fight climate change,” Turkey’s Deputy Energy and Natural Resources Minister Zafer Demircan said Monday. The summit host aims to lift electricity’s share of the nation’s final energy consumption to 36% by 2040 from about 22% currently.

Falling costs are strengthening the economic case for renewables, according to Irena. Since 2010, the levelised cost of electricity from solar PV has fallen by 89%, onshore wind by 71%, and offshore wind by 63%, the organisation said in a July report.

Disruption to oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz as a result of the Iran war has also added urgency to the deployment of renewables.

See also: India approves US$1.5 bil push for energy storage capacity

“We’re seeing more and more governments looking at what’s happening in the war and actually seeing that as a catalyst for them to really upscale renewables in their own country,” said Rebecca Williams, deputy CEO of the Global Wind Energy Council, an industry group.

More investment is needed to increase adoption of clean energy, particularly in offshore wind, where upfront costs are high, La Camera said.

Funding for renewables projects remains a constraint, according to Turkey’s Demircan. “The main thing is to find the financing,” he said.

title: New World’s top shareholder seeks bank loan as equity deal looms — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 10): Chow Tai Fook Enterprises Ltd, an investment arm of Hong Kong’s billionaire Cheng family, is seeking about HK$5 billion (US$637 million or $810 million) in fresh funding from banks, according to people familiar with the matter.

The financing would be a new-money loan and would be used for general corporate purposes, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing private matters.

The fundraising would provide CTFE, New World Development Co’s largest shareholder, with a liquidity cushion if it decides to proceed with a broad recapitalisation of the cash-strapped builder. Such a move could include a rights issue, a mechanism where existing stockholders can buy new shares in proportion to their current holdings, other people familiar with the matter said last month.

The potential new loan for CTFE could be signed as soon as this month, though details are still under discussion, the people said.

CTFE and New World didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

The Chengs have been floating capital injection proposals for months as they explore options to support New World. That’s kept investors focused on how CTFE could raise cash to back any transaction.

See also: Hong Kong bourse operator's profit falls as AI scrutiny hits listings, trading

New World is still reeling from the property downturn in mainland China and Hong Kong and reported a HK$19.7 billion (US$2.5 billion) net loss for its latest fiscal year.

The builder has been seeking approval from its bank lenders to extend by two years about HK$88 billion in loans, which were secured in Hong Kong’s largest ever debt refinancing in 2025.

See also: Hong Kong chip IPOs tap intertwined networks of investors and bosses

The company plans to repay 10% of the loan principal using proceeds from the equity injection, which it aims to complete by January.

If a rights issue does go through, it would represent a major sign of direct financial backing from the controlling family for the debt-laden company. The developer has a market capitalisation of about HK$12.8 billion as of Nov 10, down 88% from its peak in 2019.

title: Vodafone raises profit forecast after cost cutting campaign
article:
(Nov 10): Vodafone Group Plc raised its full-year profit guidance after the British phone company cut costs and the size of its workforce.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation after leases will rise to €13.2 billion (US$14.8 billion) to €13.4 billion for the fiscal year ending in March, the company said in a statement on Tuesday. That compares to the €13 billion to €13.3 billion range Vodafone had forecast in July.

Chief executive officer Margherita Della Valle has been selling assets and reducing costs, which included cutting more than 3,000 jobs across Europe in the first half, to try to reignite growth at telecom company. Most of the company’s growth comes from less saturated markets in Africa and the Middle East, while its largest units in Europe face heavy competition for subscribers.

The company said it delivered €700 million in annual gross savings between 2023 and 2026 due to staff cuts and other measures. It expects to reduce European operating expenditures by over €200 million in the 2027 fiscal year and has announced 2,300 role reductions in Germany.

Vodafone’s shares closed at 116.95 pence on Monday and have gained 18% this year.

In the UK, the company combined with CK Hutchison Holdings Ltd’s rival business Three, taking the number of large mobile operators to three from four. Vodafone took full control of the venture earlier this year, and Della Valle said the merged business would save £1 billion ($1.3 billion) annually by 2032. The extra savings will come from shutting down overlapping sites and upgrading the two networks to be more efficient, the company said last month.

See also: Infineon boosts AI sales outlook due to data centre growth plans

The company is recovering from a 2024 law change in the German market that barred landlords from bundling rent with TV and broadband services, costing the company millions of customers. Vodafone is using broadband connections to differentiate from some competitors by selling bundles with mobile services.

title: Deeper economic slump tests Marcos, Philippine Central Bank
article:
(Nov 10): A surprise slowdown in the Philippine economy has triggered calls for the central bank to go easy on interest rate increases and for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr to do more to revive growth.

Economists from China Banking Corporation, Metropolitan Bank & Trust Co, Union Bank of the Philippines and Pantheon Macroeconomics have raised the possibility that the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas will pause its rate hikes after economic growth last quarter decelerated to the weakest since the pandemic.

“It sure doesn’t make much sense to slam hard on the brakes if we’re driving uphill on rocky terrain,” Metropolitan Bank chief economist Nicholas Mapa said.

Resurgent inflation due to the protracted Iran war and farm damage from monsoon rains have further strained the consumption-driven, import-dependent economy that is already falling behind most of its Southeast Asian neighbours. Household spending, a key economic pillar, remained tepid and weighed on a swathe of industries from retail to real estate.

Reacting to the poor data, Marcos’ office on Tuesday (Nov 10) said it is working to stabilise prices of basic goods and ensure a sufficient supply of food and fuel. “We are doing everything we can. The government is not neglecting its duties,” his press officer Claire Castro said at a briefing.

See also: Canada expands US tariff exemptions, cuts some aluminium relief

The central bank has said fiscal measures are expected to help the economy recover after it surprised markets with an outsized half-point increase last month. Governor Eli Remolona last week said the BSP remains in a tightening cycle as it fights persistent price pressures.

Inflation accelerated to a higher-than-expected 7.8% in October, well above its 3% target, and Remolona last week said it will take “a few more months” to peak.

The growth outlook for this quarter, meanwhile, remains gloomy, despite a typical consumption boost during the Christmas holidays. El Niño, which alters rainfall patterns and can fuel drought, is threatening to inflict more pain on the agriculture sector, which already suffered a record slump last quarter.

See also: Vietnam turns to taxes, state borrowing to finance growth push

“Looking ahead, economic growth is likely to remain subdued through the fourth quarter before recovering toward the 4%–5% range by the first quarter of 2027,” said Domini Velasquez, chief economist at Manila-based China Banking. “Demand conditions remain clearly weak, with a sizable negative output gap.”

But Bloomberg Economics and Bank of America said the BSP is likely to stay on course with its monetary tightening cycle despite weaker growth, with looming risks to inflation including El Niño.

Complicating any shift in the central bank’s tightening policy is the peso, which has declined almost 7% this year to be Asia’s second-worst-performing currency against the dollar. The peso strengthened 0.65% on Tuesday, recovering losses from the previous day and moving in line with gains in other regional currencies.

With weak economic growth constraining the central bank’s room for rate increases, the government “must do the heavy lifting", according to Jonathan Ravelas, a senior adviser at Reyes Tacandong & Co in Manila. Officials should, in particular, increase food supply by rebuilding local production to lower prices, he said.

The worsening economic slump has also prompted businesses to call on the Marcos administration to act. The Makati Business Club — which counts senior executives of the nation’s biggest companies as members — said the government should continue to restore business confidence and accelerate infrastructure projects.

“The policy response must go beyond stimulating economic activity and attracting investments,” MBC executive director Julia Abad said in a statement. “It must strengthen governance, institutions and policy execution.”

title: Infineon boosts AI sales outlook due to data centre growth plans
article:
(Nov 10): Infineon Technologies AG raised its 2027 data centre sales forecast, signalling confidence that the business will drive growth even as investor concerns mount over the artificial intelligence boom.

The German chipmaker sees data centre sales growing to around €4 billion (US$4.5 billion) in the year that ends in September, it said in a statement on Tuesday. Previously, Infineon forecast AI data centre power solutions would make €2.5 billion in the period. It also makes about €500 million annually from traditional data centres, and the new figure comprises both segments.

“We expect a significant increase in revenue and profitability in fiscal year 2027,” chief executive officer Jochen Hanebeck said in the statement, adding power chips for data centres and electromobility would be among the growth drivers.

Concerns about a possible AI bubble have driven a steep selloff in companies from chipmakers to so-called neoclouds. Infineon’s shares have declined by 45% from a peak in June. Demand for data centre chips has helped Infineon and peers such as STMicroelectronics NV compensate for slow revenue recovery from the struggling automotive sector.

Infineon is the only one among European chipmakers to give a full year forecast. The company tends to guide cautiously and then adjust estimates as visibility improves, according to JPMorgan analysts including Sandeep Deshpande. JPMorgan had expected Infineon to guide for 2027 data center revenue, including CPU and other non-AI accelerator-related power revenue, of between €3.5 billion and €4 billion.

As the buildout of data centers around the world accelerated, demand for Infineon’s chips to control power soared. Those chips can support advanced processors such as those from Nvidia Corp that are fuelling the AI boom.

See also: Zara owner backs new fund targeting supply chain emissions

However, a punishing post-US election selloff has rippled across the industry. Some potential investors in Anthropic PBC, which can begin formal marketing of its initial public offering as soon as Tuesday, discussed a valuation ranging from about US$1.1 trillion to US$1.3 trillion, well below where talks had been focused just a month ago, Bloomberg News reported last week.

Infineon’s fiscal 2026 revenue was €16.35 billion, matching analysts’ estimates, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The company sees sales growing to about €20 billion in the current year. The board will propose increasing the 2026 dividend by three cents to €0.38.

Infineon said its adjusted gross margin will be in the mid-to-high forties percentage range in the period and it plans investments of €3 billion to €3.5 billion. Adjusted gross margin was 43.1% in fiscal 2026.

See also: Vodacom profit jumps 26% as Safaricom gains boost earnings

The main areas of investment will be equipment for the ramp-up of production at Infineon’s Dresden site in Germany, the expansion of silicon carbide capacities in Malaysia, and the start of gallium nitride manufacturing on 300-millimetre wafers in the Austrian town of Villach.

Infineon is also considering setting up wafer fabrication in Thailand, although such a move is unlikely in the next three years. In September, Infineon announced it will sell parts of its memory business to focus on its core activities and more dynamic parts of its portfolio.

title: FWD Private issues US$318 million insurance policy
article:
On Nov 10, FWD Private (Bermuda) announced that it has achieved a new GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS™ title for the most valuable life insurance policy. Valued at US$318 million (issued in Hong Kong), the policy issued by FWD Private provides a tailored, comprehensive solution that supports an individual customer’s wealth preservation and intergenerational legacy planning.

Established in 2023, FWD Private offers comprehensive legacy planning solutions and services for high-net-worth (HNW) and ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) individuals.

Shelyne Shum, Chief Partnership Distribution Officer, FWD Private, said, "This record-breaking policy marks an important milestone for FWD and reflects the trust that HNW customers place in us. It further reinforces FWD’s leadership in the HNW segment and demonstrates our proven capabilities across wealth and legacy planning and protection strategies. Building on our strong foundation, FWD Private continues to accelerate growth across Asia and deliver tailored legacy planning solutions that empower customers and their families to truly celebrate living.”

She added, "A case of this scale and complexity calls for tremendous collaboration. My heartfelt thanks go to our external partners, including broker adviser Charles Monat Associates, private bank and reinsurers, as well as internal teams across distribution, case management, product solutions, underwriting and corporate governance, for their dedication and collective effort in delivering this remarkable policy. This achievement is also a testament to the strength of our distribution network and the deep partnerships we have built across the industry.”

Teddy Chu, Chief Executive Officer, Hong Kong, Charles Monat Associates, said, “We are incredibly proud to contribute to this new GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS™ title of the most valuable life insurance policy for the second consecutive time, led by the same Charles Monat Associates consultant. Our track record and experience in advising clients on complex solutions has played a key role in supporting the appropriate legacy solution for this remarkable case. This new record policy underscores Hong Kong's position as one of the world's leading wealth management and life insurance hub, reinforcing the importance of collaboration among brokers, insurers, and bank partners to address the evolving wealth planning needs of HNW and UHNW individuals.”

title: Insurers react to riot risks across Europe by capping coverage
article:
(Nov 10): Insurers are taking steps to limit their exposure to the risk of losses tied to a wave of street protests in cities across Europe.

The industry has started imposing caps on coverage, raising deductibles and — in some high-risk locations — eliminating coverage altogether, according to Marcos Alvarez, who oversees global insurance at Morningstar DBRS.

Such risks, which fall into the insurance category of strikes, riots and civil commotion (SRCC), have been on the rise in Europe in recent years. And according to Allianz SE, Europe’s biggest insurer, companies increasingly need to treat SRCC as a risk not just associated with emerging markets but also with high-income countries.

The development has been on full display across the continent in recent weeks, as student protests that started in France morphed into region-wide demonstrations centred on a wide range of basic affordability issues. Anger over planned data centres is also leading to protests. As civil unrest continues, industry insiders are starting to draw parallels between SRCC risks and the kind of damage that’s normally associated with natural disasters like hurricanes, Alvarez said.

“Because of the severity and the magnitude of losses, SRCC is now behaving like a natural catastrophe,” he said. “These aren’t secondary threats anymore.”

Nicolas Aubert, CEO of Howden France, says the changing face of SRCC is now “actively reshaping” coverage terms.

See also: Thailand shifts disaster risk to insurers with US$467 mil plan

“Insurers have had to move quickly to speed up claims payments and support affected businesses,” he said. “The strain shows in tighter terms — higher deductibles, lower limits and coverage restrictions", all of which is “leaving some policyholders exposed".

More than half a million people took part in marches across France in mid-October, with violence and looting disrupting demonstrations and damaging public buildings and stores. Since then, police dramatically stepped up their presence and requirements were introduced in an effort to keep marches free of violence. Protests have also gripped cities in Germany, Belgium and Portugal as affordability issues fuel widespread discontent.

Ian Humphries, who heads Allianz’s political violence and terrorism unit in London, says the insurer isn’t applying “any broad reactive restrictions” based on the latest protests. Instead, coverage is done on a “case-by-case underwriting basis” and takes into account factors such as “proximity to areas that may be more susceptible to civil unrest", he said.

See also: Great Eastern investing in Granite Private Credit Fund — Bloomberg

The insurance industry has sought to keep up with the rise in SRCC risks by developing tools to help measure the new landscape. In September, Howden launched an analytics programme called UNREST to give insurers and reinsurers access to more recent data on the impact of strikes, riots and civil unrest.

Howden says its model helps insurers identify where exposures are concentrated, how events might unfold and the potential portfolio impacts. SRCC threats are becoming more frequent and localised, and older models don’t adequately capture the real risks insurers now face, the broker said.

While SRCC coverage has historically been offered as a standard part of commercial policies, insurers are now treating such risks separately to reflect the potential for significant losses, according to AM Best, a credit-rating firm specialised in the insurance industry.

“As evidenced by multibillion-dollar losses from the unrest in Minneapolis and New Caledonia in 2020 and 2024, the 2025 Nepal riots, and the recent widespread destruction in France, SRCC events can have a significant impact,” Mathilde Jakobsen, senior director at AM Best, said in a recent note.

Protests in France have so far disproportionately affected commercial premises and public buildings, with insured losses expected to be below €1.2 billion to cover, according to Morningstar DBRS. The figure may yet be revised higher if the unrest continues.

“Typical riots were concentrated in one city for a couple of days, but now the violence is being correlated across a country or even across several countries,” Alvarez said. “When you have losses from lots of properties at the same time, that puts a different type of strain on insurers’ capital, earnings and capital ratios.”

Verisk Maplecroft, which models SRCC catastrophe risk, describes the protests in Europe as the “most significant concurrent unrest” seen in the region in years. Verisk’s risk gauge for large-scale unrest in Europe is currently at its highest since 2021.
